import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { ALERT_RULES, ORDER_RULES, REPLY_AIM_HOURS, STANDING_RULES } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK, RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK } from "../src/screens/Home";

/**
 * The README's moderation runbook and the console's home screen say the same thing (3c design, section 13, Task 12).
 * When decided items wait for the daily release longer than it ever takes, or an erasure is more than a day late, the
 * home screen shows the count with the runbook's sentence for it, and each sentence is a constant of the screen. This
 * test reads README.md from the repository's root and holds the runbook to the same two constants, word for word, so
 * that what staff are told on the screen is what the operator reads in the runbook: whoever changes one changes both.
 */
const README = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..", "..", "..", "README.md");

/** Markdown's code mark. The README sets a log line or a setting in code marks; the console shows the same words as plain text. */
const CODE_MARK = "`";

/** A text as its reader sees it: without the code marks. Nothing else is changed, so every word and every sign must agree. */
const withoutCodeMarks = (text: string): string => text.split(CODE_MARK).join("");

/** The README's lines, as written. */
function readmeLines(): string[] {
  return readFileSync(README, "utf8").split("\n");
}

/** The lines of the README's section "Moderation": from its heading to the next heading of the same level. */
function moderationSection(): string[] {
  const lines = readmeLines();
  const start = lines.indexOf("## Moderation");
  if (start === -1) return [];
  const rest = lines.slice(start + 1);
  const end = rest.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith("## "));
  return end === -1 ? rest : rest.slice(0, end);
}

/** The section's runbook as its reader sees it: every line after "The runbook:", without the code marks. */
function moderationRunbook(): string {
  const section = moderationSection();
  const start = section.indexOf("The runbook:");
  return start === -1 ? "" : withoutCodeMarks(section.slice(start + 1).join("\n"));
}

/** How often `part` stands in `text`. */
const count = (text: string, part: string): number => text.split(part).length - 1;

describe("the README's moderation runbook says what the home screen says", () => {
  const sentences: [string, string][] = [
    ["decisions not released", RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK],
    ["late erasures", ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK],
  ];

  test("the README has a section Moderation, and the section has a runbook", () => {
    expect(readmeLines()).toContain("## Moderation");
    expect(moderationSection()).toContain("The runbook:");
    expect(moderationRunbook().trim()).not.toBe("");
  });

  test("neither constant holds a code mark or a line break, so reading the README without its code marks hides no difference", () => {
    for (const [name, sentence] of sentences) {
      expect(sentence, name).not.toContain(CODE_MARK);
      expect(sentence, name).not.toContain("\n");
      // A whole sentence: it opens with "A count of" and ends in a full stop, as the runbook's bullet writes it.
      expect(sentence.startsWith("A count of "), name).toBe(true);
      expect(sentence.endsWith("."), name).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  for (const [name, sentence] of sentences) {
    test(`the runbook holds the home screen's sentence for ${name}, word for word`, () => {
      expect(moderationRunbook()).toContain(sentence);
    });

    test(`the sentence for ${name} stands once in the README, in that runbook: no second copy can drift from it`, () => {
      expect(count(withoutCodeMarks(readmeLines().join("\n")), sentence)).toBe(1);
      expect(count(moderationRunbook(), sentence)).toBe(1);
    });
  }

  test("both sentences stand in one bullet of the runbook, the release's first, as the home screen orders its two lines", () => {
    const bullets = moderationRunbook()
      .split("\n")
      .filter((line) => line.includes(RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK) || line.includes(ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK));
    expect(bullets).toHaveLength(1);
    const bullet = bullets[0] ?? "";
    expect(bullet.startsWith("- ")).toBe(true);
    expect(bullet.indexOf(RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK)).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(bullet.indexOf(ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK)).toBeGreaterThan(bullet.indexOf(RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK));
  });
});

/**
 * The README's account sanctions (3e design, section 13, Task 7) and the constants they print. The section Moderation
 * describes 3e in a paragraph that opens with ACCOUNT_SANCTIONS_LEAD and a bullet for each title below, and its runbook
 * gains the bullets of section 13's (a) to (h). Every number in that text is a number of STANDING_RULES or
 * REPLY_AIM_HOURS: a table holds each in its sentence, and every other run of digits is refused, so the README cannot
 * keep a number the constants changed. A bullet added to 3e's text joins its list here.
 */
const ACCOUNT_SANCTIONS_LEAD = "Account sanctions (sub-project 3e;";
const STANDING_TITLES = [
  "Strikes.",
  "The ladder.",
  "Announced suspensions and the reply.",
  "Suspensions at once.",
  "While suspended.",
  "Termination.",
  "The restriction of reporting.",
  "Handle retirement.",
  "What is kept of them.",
  "The Standing screen.",
  // The runbook's bullets (a) to (h).
  "Account sanctions each working day.",
  "Answering a reply.",
  "A protective suspension.",
  "A breach that lies only in a handle",
  "A notice a person did not get by mail.",
  "A measure at once while an announced suspension waits.",
  "A mark that was wrong.",
  "Reports before an account measure.",
] as const;

/** The lines of 3e's text in Moderation, without code marks: the lead paragraph and each bullet by its bold title. */
function standingLines(): { lead: string | undefined; bullets: Map<string, string[]> } {
  const section = moderationSection().map(withoutCodeMarks);
  const bullets = new Map(STANDING_TITLES.map((title) => [title as string, section.filter((line) => line.startsWith(`- **${title}`))]));
  return { lead: section.find((line) => line.startsWith(ACCOUNT_SANCTIONS_LEAD)), bullets };
}
const standingText = (): string => {
  const { lead, bullets } = standingLines();
  return [lead ?? "", ...[...bullets.values()].flat()].join("\n");
};

/** A number in a sentence as the README writes it, and the constant it is. */
const S = STANDING_RULES;
const STANDING_NUMBERS: { constant: string; phrase: string }[] = [
  { constant: "strikeDays", phrase: `which counts for ${S.strikeDays} days` },
  { constant: "ladderStrikes", phrase: `With ${S.ladderStrikes} active strikes` },
  { constant: "ladderDays", phrase: `a suspension of at most ${S.ladderDays[0]} days, then ${S.ladderDays[1]}, then ${S.ladderDays[2]}` },
  { constant: "ladderMemoryDays", phrase: `the ladder suspensions decided in the last ${S.ladderMemoryDays} days` },
  { constant: "replyWindowHours", phrase: `The suspension starts ${S.replyWindowHours} hours after korbat's relay accepted the notice mail` },
  { constant: "undeliveredHours", phrase: `or ${S.undeliveredHours} hours after the decision` },
  { constant: "threatDays", phrase: `(up to ${S.threatDays} days), terrorist content` },
  { constant: "terroristDays", phrase: `likewise (up to ${S.terroristDays} days)` },
  { constant: "floodPosts", phrase: `at least ${S.floodPosts} posts in the last` },
  { constant: "floodMinutes", phrase: `posts in the last ${S.floodMinutes} minutes` },
  { constant: "floodDays", phrase: `minutes (up to ${S.floodDays} days)` },
  { constant: "basisAgeDays", phrase: `at most ${S.basisAgeDays} days old` },
  { constant: "protectiveDays", phrase: `once for that seal (up to ${S.protectiveDays} days)` },
  { constant: "protectiveDays", phrase: `for at most ${S.protectiveDays} days, never worded as a finding` },
  { constant: "reportWarnMarks", phrase: `At least ${S.reportWarnMarks} marked reports in ${S.reportFrameDays} days` },
  { constant: "reportRestrictMarks", phrase: `${S.reportRestrictMarks} marked reports sent after it, while it counts (${S.reportFrameDays} days)` },
  { constant: "reportRestrictDays", phrase: `open a restriction of at most ${S.reportRestrictDays} days` },
  { constant: "reportFrameDays", phrase: `the marks and the daily tallies ${S.reportFrameDays} days after their report's UTC day` },
  { constant: "REPLY_AIM_HOURS", phrase: `korbat aims to answer a reply to one within ${REPLY_AIM_HOURS} hours` },
  { constant: "REPLY_AIM_HOURS", phrase: `answer within ${REPLY_AIM_HOURS} hours` },
];

describe("the README's account sanctions say what the constants say (3e design, section 13, Task 7)", () => {
  test("Moderation opens 3e's part with its paragraph, and each of its bullets stands there once", () => {
    const { lead, bullets } = standingLines();
    expect(lead).toBeDefined();
    for (const [title, lines] of bullets) expect(lines, title).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  test("the runbook holds the bullets of section 13's (a) to (h), after The runbook: and before the records kept off the server", () => {
    const runbook = moderationRunbook().split("\n");
    for (const title of STANDING_TITLES.slice(STANDING_TITLES.indexOf("Account sanctions each working day."))) expect(runbook.some((line) => line.startsWith(`- **${title}`)), title).toBe(true);
  });

  test("every number of 3e's text stands in its sentence with the constant's value", () => {
    const text = standingText();
    for (const row of STANDING_NUMBERS) expect(text, `${row.constant}: ${row.phrase}`).toContain(row.phrase);
    // The table names every member of STANDING_RULES but the share, which the text writes as a word.
    expect([...new Set(STANDING_NUMBERS.map((row) => row.constant))].sort()).toEqual([...Object.keys(S).filter((key) => key !== "reportWarnShare"), "REPLY_AIM_HOURS"].sort());
    expect(S.reportWarnShare).toBe(0.5);
    expect(text).toContain("being at least half of the person's rule reports then");
  });

  test("and no other number: every run of digits in it is a constant's, outside the names of sub-projects, rules, articles and the design's file", () => {
    const values = new Set<string>([...Object.values(S).flat(), REPLY_AIM_HOURS].map(String));
    const outside = standingText()
      .replace(/docs\/superpowers\/specs\/[0-9a-z-]+\.md/g, " ")
      .replace(/\b[0-9][a-f]\b/g, " ")
      .replace(/\bR[1-6]\b/g, " ")
      .replace(/Art\. [0-9]+(\([0-9]+\))?(\([a-z]\))?/g, " ");
    expect((outside.match(/[0-9]+/g) ?? []).filter((digits) => !values.has(digits))).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("the lines 3e made false are gone: the handle left open for 3e, formula version 1 and the mails that name 3e", () => {
    const all = readmeLines().join("\n");
    expect(all).not.toContain("the case stays open for sub-project 3e's handle retirement");
    expect(all).not.toContain("Until sub-project 3e's formula version 2");
    expect(all).not.toContain("EXPLORE_V1");
    expect(all).not.toContain("still names sub-project 3e");
    // The hard gate names 3f's order path and 3d's handling of sealed images, as it did since 3e's design.
    expect(all).toContain("until sub-project 3f's order path and sub-project 3d's handling of sealed images have both shipped");
  });
});

/**
 * The README's authorities' orders (3f design, section 13, Task 7; W.9 and W.10) and the constants they print. 3f's text
 * is the section "Authorities' orders", Upgrading from its 3f paragraph on (Task 1), Restoring's block "Restoring with
 * the keeper's copy" (Task 6) and Before going public's owner's list. Every number in it is a number of ORDER_RULES or
 * ALERT_RULES: a table holds each in its sentence, and every other run of digits is refused but for what names a
 * reference (an article, a research finding, a row of the design's section 2, a check P1 to P8, a list's numbering, a
 * path, a date), so the README cannot keep a number the constants changed. A setting is written as the operator sets it
 * in infra/.env, an API setting with the prefix Compose maps. A section added to 3f's text joins its list here.
 */
const FENCE = "```";

/** The lines of a "## " section of the README, from its heading to the next heading of the same level. */
function sectionLines(heading: string): string[] {
  const lines = readmeLines();
  const start = lines.indexOf(heading);
  if (start === -1) return [];
  const rest = lines.slice(start + 1);
  const end = rest.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith("## "));
  return end === -1 ? rest : rest.slice(0, end);
}
/** A section's lines from the first that begins with these words to the section's end, or to the first that begins with `until`. */
function linesFrom(lines: string[], lead: string, until?: string): string[] {
  const start = lines.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith(lead));
  if (start === -1) return [];
  const rest = lines.slice(start);
  const end = until === undefined ? -1 : rest.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith(until));
  return end === -1 ? rest : rest.slice(0, end);
}
/** Lines without their fenced code: a command's own numbers and words are not the runbook's. */
function withoutFences(lines: string[]): string[] {
  let inside = false;
  return lines.filter((line) => {
    if (line.startsWith(FENCE)) {
      inside = !inside;
      return false;
    }
    return !inside;
  });
}

const ORDERS_HEADING = "## Authorities' orders";
const ORDERS_TITLES = [
  "The contact point.",
  "On call.",
  "A removal order, step by step",
  "Other messages and orders.",
  "When nobody can act within the hour.",
  "Notifications and hand-overs.",
  "A person asks about a missing post.",
  "An author writes about an order's notice.",
  "The daily copy.",
  "A key in someone else's hands.",
  "The yearly counts.",
] as const;
const OWNERS_LEAD = "**The owner's list (sub-project 3f).**";
const OWNERS_TITLES = [
  "The Member State.",
  "The mailbox.",
  "The people's own access to the mailbox.",
  "Registering.",
  "The push hostname and ntfy's users.",
  "The phones.",
  "The keys.",
  "The papers, and counsel.",
  "The contact address.",
  "The page for the yearly report.",
  "The keeper, and the two places files rest.",
  "Decide",
  "Counsel",
] as const;

/** 3f's text, part by part, without code marks and fenced code. */
function ordersParts(): Record<"orders" | "upgrading" | "restoring" | "owners", string> {
  const read = (lines: string[]) => withoutCodeMarks(withoutFences(lines).join("\n"));
  return {
    orders: read(sectionLines(ORDERS_HEADING)),
    upgrading: read(linesFrom(sectionLines("## Upgrading"), "Authorities' orders and the alert channel (sub-project 3f)")),
    restoring: read(linesFrom(sectionLines("## Restoring"), "**Restoring with the keeper's copy**")),
    owners: read(linesFrom(sectionLines("## Before going public"), OWNERS_LEAD, "Set these in")),
  };
}
const ordersText = (): string => Object.values(ordersParts()).join("\n");

/** A number in a sentence as the README writes it, and the constant it is. */
const O = ORDER_RULES;
const A = ALERT_RULES;
const ORDER_NUMBERS: { constant: string; part: keyof ReturnType<typeof ordersParts>; phrase: string }[] = [
  { constant: "ALERT_RULES.pollSeconds", part: "orders", phrase: `reads the inbox and the junk folder every ${A.pollSeconds} seconds` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.escalateMinutes", part: "orders", phrase: `it rings every staff phone ${O.escalateMinutes} minutes after its arrival` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.itemsPerAction", part: "orders", phrase: `one key touch for up to ${O.itemsPerAction} posts` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.holdWarningDays", part: "orders", phrase: `alerted daily in the last ${O.holdWarningDays} days before any release` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.reportHoldDays", part: "orders", phrase: `the address is kept for at most ${O.reportHoldDays} days` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.reportHoldDays", part: "upgrading", phrase: `keeps its address, and nothing else, for at most ${O.reportHoldDays} days` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.copyOverdueHours", part: "orders", phrase: `once the newest copy is more than ${O.copyOverdueHours} hours old` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.quietMinutes", part: "owners", phrase: `bounded only by the quiet period of ${O.quietMinutes} minutes` },
];

/** What names a reference and is no number of the runbook's, taken out before the digits are counted; only the second keeps a group, the character before the name. */
const REFERENCES: RegExp[] = [
  // A path, a file or a regulation's number: whatever holds a slash.
  /[A-Za-z0-9_.()-]*[/][A-Za-z0-9_./-]+/g,
  // A sub-project's name (3f, 3d, 1b) and a phone check (P1 to P8).
  /(^|[^0-9A-Za-z])([0-9][a-f]|P[1-8])(?=[^0-9A-Za-z]|$)/gm,
  // A list's numbering.
  /^[0-9]+[.] /gm,
  // An article of an act, with its paragraphs.
  /Art(?:icle|[.]) [0-9]+(?:[(][0-9a-z]+[)])*/g,
  // A finding of the research, with its questions; a row of the design's section 2, and the section itself.
  /(?:OL|AU) E[0-9]+[.][0-9]+(?: questions [0-9]+ to [0-9]+)?/g,
  /[(]rows? [0-9]+(?: and [0-9]+)?[)]/g,
  /section [0-9]+/g,
  // A step of a list named in a sentence.
  /steps? [0-9]+/g,
  // An instant as an example of the form, a date of the year, the hand-over's user, a hash's name, a status's code.
  /[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:]+Z/g,
  /[0-9]+ March/g,
  /uid [0-9]+/g,
  /sha256/g,
  /answers 503/g,
];

describe("the README's authorities' orders say what the constants say (3f design, section 13, Task 7; W.9 and W.10)", () => {
  test("the README has the section Authorities' orders after Moderation, and each of its parts stands there once, in W.9's order", () => {
    const lines = readmeLines();
    expect(lines.indexOf(ORDERS_HEADING)).toBeGreaterThan(lines.indexOf("## Moderation"));
    const section = sectionLines(ORDERS_HEADING).map(withoutCodeMarks);
    const at = ORDERS_TITLES.map((title) => section.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith(`**${title}`)));
    for (const title of ORDERS_TITLES) expect(section.filter((line) => line.startsWith(`**${title}`)), title).toHaveLength(1);
    expect([...at].sort((a, b) => a - b)).toEqual(at);
  });

  test("Before going public holds the owner's list of thirteen, each line by its title, in W.10's order", () => {
    const owners = linesFrom(sectionLines("## Before going public"), OWNERS_LEAD, "Set these in").filter((line) => /^[0-9]+[.] /.test(line));
    expect(owners.map((line) => line.slice(0, line.indexOf(" ")))).toEqual(OWNERS_TITLES.map((_, n) => `${n + 1}.`));
    for (const [n, title] of OWNERS_TITLES.entries()) expect(owners[n]!.startsWith(`${n + 1}. **${title}`), title).toBe(true);
  });

  test("every number of 3f's text stands in its sentence with the constant's value", () => {
    const parts = ordersParts();
    for (const row of ORDER_NUMBERS) expect(parts[row.part], `${row.constant}: ${row.phrase}`).toContain(row.phrase);
  });

  test("and no other number: every run of digits in it is a constant's, outside what names a reference", () => {
    const values = new Set<string>([...Object.values(O), ...Object.values(A)].filter((value) => typeof value === "number").map(String));
    const outside = REFERENCES.reduce((text, pattern) => text.replace(pattern, (_match: string, lead: unknown) => (typeof lead === "string" ? `${lead} ` : " ")), ordersText());
    expect((outside.match(/[0-9]+/g) ?? []).filter((digits) => !values.has(digits))).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("a setting is written as the operator sets it in infra/.env: an API setting with its prefix", () => {
    const withMarks = [sectionLines(ORDERS_HEADING), linesFrom(sectionLines("## Upgrading"), "Authorities' orders and the alert channel"), linesFrom(sectionLines("## Restoring"), "**Restoring with the keeper's copy**")]
      .flatMap((lines) => withoutFences(lines))
      .join("\n");
    for (const name of ["NOTIFY", "REPORT_HOLD", "MODERATION_RETENTION", "HOME_STATE", "CONTACT_POINT", "PUSH_ORIGIN", "APP_ORIGIN"]) {
      expect(withMarks.includes(`${CODE_MARK}${name}`), name).toBe(false);
    }
    for (const name of ["API_CONTACT_POINT", "API_HOME_STATE", "API_REPORT_HOLD", "API_MODERATION_RETENTION", "APP_SITE", "COMPOSE_PROFILES", "WEB_CONTACT_POINT", "WEB_HOME_STATE"]) {
      expect(withMarks.includes(name) || ordersText().includes(name), name).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test("the hand-over's and the yearly counts' commands stand in the runbook as the operator types them", () => {
    const orders = ordersParts().orders;
    for (const words of [
      "docker compose --profile handover run --rm -T -v <directory>:/handover handover < list > digests",
      "handover-list",
      "handover-record",
      "handover-destroyed",
      "staff.js tco-counts <last year>",
      "docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js address-check --handle <handle> < address",
    ]) {
      expect(orders, words).toContain(words);
    }
    expect(readmeLines().join("\n")).toContain("docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm migrate node dist/staff.js tco-counts <year>");
  });

  test("the lines 3f made false are gone, and the hard gate reads as W.10 words it", () => {
    const all = readmeLines().join("\n");
    expect(all).not.toContain("Until sub-project 3f's off-server copy of decisions");
    expect(all).not.toContain("take the app's public hostname off the tunnel and leave the console's on");
    expect(all).not.toContain("staff.js account-facts");
    expect(all).not.toContain("account-facts <handle>");
    expect(all).not.toContain("Authorities' orders before 3f.");
    expect(all).not.toContain("in their own records until sub-project 3f");
    expect(all).not.toContain("With sub-project 3f the authorities' contact address is published as well");
    expect(all).toContain("until sub-project 3f's order path and sub-project 3d's handling of sealed images have both shipped and the list below is done");
  });
});
````

import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { STAFF_USAGE, enrollSettings, migratorUrl, parseStaffArgs, revokeSettings, runStaffCommand, staffDatabaseUrls } from "../src/cli/staff";

const HASH_A = "ab".repeat(32);
const HASH_B = "0123456789abcdef".repeat(4);
const API_URL = "postgres://korbat_api:x@localhost:5432/korbat";
const AUTH_URL = "postgres://korbat_auth:x@localhost:5432/korbat";

/** The command's lines, each marked with the stream it went to. */
function capture() {
  const lines: string[] = [];
  return { lines, out: { log: (line: string) => lines.push(`out ${line}`), error: (line: string) => lines.push(`err ${line}`) } };
}

describe("staff.js arguments", () => {
  test("the usage lists the commands that exist", () => {
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toMatch(/^usage: node dist\/staff\.js <command>/);
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("enroll <email>");
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("keys [<email>]");
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("audit-head");
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("audit-verify [<chain_seq>:<hash> ...]");
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("revoke <email> <key id>");
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("revoke <email> all");
    // enroll runs as the migrator, in the migrate service; the usage says where.
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toMatch(/run --rm migrate node dist\/staff\.js enroll/);
  });

  test("reads revoke with an email address and a key id or all, normalising both", () => {

    for (const key of ["ALL", "every", "12", `${id}0`, id.replace(/-/g, "")]) {
      expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["revoke", "mod@korbat.local", key]), key).toThrow(`not a key id or all: ${key}`);
    }
  });

  test("reads enroll with one email address and keys with one or none, normalising the address", () => {
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["enroll", " Mod@Korbat.Local "])).toEqual({ command: "enroll", email: "mod@korbat.local" });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["keys"])).toEqual({ command: "keys", email: null });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["keys", "Mod@Korbat.Local"])).toEqual({ command: "keys", email: "mod@korbat.local" });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["enroll"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["enroll", "a@b.io", "b@c.io"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["keys", "a@b.io", "b@c.io"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["enroll", "moderator"])).toThrow(`not an email address: moderator\n${STAFF_USAGE}`);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["keys", "all"])).toThrow(`not an email address: all\n${STAFF_USAGE}`);
  });

  test("reads audit-head, and audit-verify with any number of kept places", () => {
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["audit-head"])).toEqual({ command: "audit-head" });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["audit-verify"])).toEqual({ command: "audit-verify", kept: [] });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["audit-verify", `12:${HASH_A}`, `3:${HASH_B}`])).toEqual({
      command: "audit-verify",
      kept: [
        { seq: 12, hash: HASH_A },
        { seq: 3, hash: HASH_B },
      ],
    });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["audit-verify", `999999999999999:${HASH_A}`]).command).toBe("audit-verify");
  });

  test("prints the usage for no command, an unknown one or extra arguments", () => {
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs([])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["audit-tail"])).toThrow(`unknown command: audit-tail\n${STAFF_USAGE}`);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["audit-head", `1:${HASH_A}`])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
  });

  test("refuses a kept place that is not <chain_seq>:<hash>, a positive place and a lower-case sha256", () => {
    for (const pair of [
      "12",
      `12 ${HASH_A}`,
      `0:${HASH_A}`,
      `-1:${HASH_A}`,
      `01:${HASH_A}`,
      `1.5:${HASH_A}`,
      `1e3:${HASH_A}`,
      `1000000000000000:${HASH_A}`,
      "12:abc",
      `12:${HASH_A.toUpperCase()}`,
      `12:${HASH_A}0`,
      `12:${HASH_A}:1`,
    ]) {
      expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["audit-verify", pair]), pair).toThrow(`not a kept place: ${pair}`);
    }
  });

  test("run without arguments, it prints its usage and answers 2 before reading any configuration", async () => {
    const { lines, out } = capture();
    expect(await runStaffCommand([], {}, out)).toBe(2);
    expect(lines).toEqual([`err ${STAFF_USAGE}`]);
  });
});

// audit-head and audit-verify need no server secret and no console configuration (3a design, section 7), so each reads
// only the database URLs it connects with, never the API's whole configuration.
describe("what each staff.js command reads of the environment", () => {
  test("audit-head reads DATABASE_URL_API alone, and audit-verify that and DATABASE_URL_AUTH", () => {
    expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "audit-head" }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL })).toEqual({ api: API_URL, auth: null });
    expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "audit-verify", kept: [] }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL })).toEqual({
      api: API_URL,
      auth: AUTH_URL,
    });
  });

  test("a setting the API's configuration would refuse, the console's included, changes nothing", () => {
    for (const extra of [
      // Not an origin as browsers send it (the final slash).
      { CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "https://console.example/" },
      // The console on the app's own origin.
      { APP_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8081", CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8081" },
      { CONSOLE_RP_ID: "not a domain" },
      // A secret too short, and production's rules over a development setup.
      { NODE_ENV: "production", AUTH_HMAC_KEY: "c2hvcnQ=", APP_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8081" },
    ]) {
      const env = { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, ...extra };
      expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "audit-verify", kept: [] }, env), JSON.stringify(extra)).toEqual({ api: API_URL, auth: AUTH_URL });
      expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "audit-head" }, env), JSON.stringify(extra)).toEqual({ api: API_URL, auth: null });
    }
  });

  test("names the database URL that is missing or not a PostgreSQL URL, and no other setting", () => {
    const cases: [Parameters<typeof staffDatabaseUrls>[0], Record<string, string>, RegExp][] = [
      [{ command: "audit-head" }, {}, /DATABASE_URL_API/],
      [{ command: "audit-head" }, { DATABASE_URL_API: "mysql://korbat:x@localhost/korbat" }, /DATABASE_URL_API/],
      [{ command: "audit-verify", kept: [] }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL }, /DATABASE_URL_AUTH/],
      [{ command: "audit-verify", kept: [] }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: "not a url" }, /DATABASE_URL_AUTH/],
    ];
    for (const [command, env, named] of cases) {
      let message = "";
      try {
        staffDatabaseUrls(command, env);
      } catch (err) {
        message = (err as Error).message;
      }
      expect(message, JSON.stringify(env)).toMatch(named);
      expect(message).toMatch(new RegExp(`^Invalid environment for ${command.command}:`));
      expect(message).not.toMatch(/APP_ORIGIN|REDIS_URL|AUTH_HMAC_KEY|SMTP_URL|CONSOLE_ORIGIN/);
    }
  });

  test("keys reads DATABASE_URL_AUTH for the keys and DATABASE_URL_API for the handles, and nothing else", () => {
    expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "keys", email: null }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "not an origin" })).toEqual({
      api: API_URL,
      auth: AUTH_URL,
    });
    expect(() => staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "keys", email: "a@b.io" }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL })).toThrow(/^Invalid environment for keys:[\s\S]*DATABASE_URL_AUTH/);
  });

  test("run with a database URL missing, it names it and answers 1", async () => {
    const { lines, out } = capture();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["audit-verify"], { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL }, out)).toBe(1);
    expect(lines).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(lines[0]).toMatch(/^err Invalid environment for audit-verify:/);
    expect(lines[0]).toContain("DATABASE_URL_AUTH");
    expect(lines[0]).not.toMatch(/APP_ORIGIN|REDIS_URL|AUTH_HMAC_KEY/);
  });
});

// enroll runs in the migrate service as the migrator (3a design, section 7): it reads the migrator's database URL and the
// console's origin and relying party ID, which Compose gives that service, and nothing of the API's configuration.
describe("what staff.js enroll reads of the environment", () => {
  const MIGRATE_URL = "postgres://korbat_migrate:x@localhost:5432/korbat";

  test("DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE, CONSOLE_ORIGIN and CONSOLE_RP_ID, the relying party ID defaulting to the console's hostname", () => {
    expect(enrollSettings({ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090" })).toEqual({
      migrate: MIGRATE_URL,
      consoleOrigin: "http://localhost:8090",
      consoleRpId: "localhost",
    });
    // A blank relying party ID, as Compose passes an empty line of infra/.env, counts as unset.
    expect(enrollSettings({ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "https://console.example", CONSOLE_RP_ID: " " }).consoleRpId).toBe("console.example");
    expect(enrollSettings({ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "https://console.example", CONSOLE_RP_ID: "Console.Example" }).consoleRpId).toBe("console.example");
  });

  test("a setting only the API reads, or one the API's configuration would refuse, changes nothing", () => {
    const env = {
      DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL,
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090",
      // The console on the app's own hostname is refused by the API's rules in production, not here.
      APP_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8081",
      NODE_ENV: "production",
      AUTH_HMAC_KEY: "c2hvcnQ=",
    };
    expect(enrollSettings(env)).toEqual({ migrate: MIGRATE_URL, consoleOrigin: "http://localhost:8090", consoleRpId: "localhost" });
  });

  test("while CONSOLE_ORIGIN is unset or blank it refuses, naming it", () => {
    for (const env of [{ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL }, { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "" }, { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "  " }]) {
      expect(() => enrollSettings(env), JSON.stringify(env)).toThrow(/CONSOLE_ORIGIN is not set: the staff console is off, so no enrolment link can be issued/);
    }
  });

  test("names the setting that is wrong, and no other", () => {
    const cases: [Record<string, string>, RegExp][] = [
      [{ CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090" }, /DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE/],
      [{ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: "mysql://x@localhost/k", CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090" }, /DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE/],
      // Not an origin as browsers send it: the staff gate would refuse every write the console makes.
      [{ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090/" }, /CONSOLE_ORIGIN/],
      [{ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090", CONSOLE_RP_ID: "http://localhost" }, /CONSOLE_RP_ID/],
    ];
    for (const [env, named] of cases) {
      let message = "";
      try {
        enrollSettings(env);
      } catch (err) {
        message = (err as Error).message;
      }
      expect(message, JSON.stringify(env)).toMatch(named);
      expect(message).toMatch(/^Invalid environment for enroll:/);
      expect(message).not.toMatch(/APP_ORIGIN|REDIS_URL|AUTH_HMAC_KEY|SMTP_URL|DATABASE_URL_API|DATABASE_URL_AUTH/);
    }
  });

  test("run while CONSOLE_ORIGIN is unset, it says so, answers 1 and connects to nothing", async () => {
    const { lines, out } = capture();
    // Nothing listens on port 1: a connection attempt would fail with another message, or hang.
    const started = Date.now();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["enroll", "mod@korbat.local"], { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: "postgres://korbat_migrate:x@127.0.0.1:1/korbat" }, out)).toBe(1);
    expect(Date.now() - started).toBeLessThan(2_000);
    expect(lines).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(lines[0]).toMatch(/^err .*CONSOLE_ORIGIN is not set/);
  });
});

// revoke runs like grant-role, in the api service (3a design, section 7): it revokes on the auth role and mails the key's
// owner, so it reads the auth role's URL and the mail settings, and nothing else of the API's configuration.
describe("what staff.js revoke reads of the environment", () => {
  const MAIL = { SMTP_URL: "smtp://localhost:1025", MAIL_FROM: "korbat <no-reply@korbat.local>" };

  test("DATABASE_URL_AUTH, SMTP_URL and MAIL_FROM, with TLS required from a plain relay in production as the API requires it", () => {
    expect(revokeSettings({ DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, ...MAIL })).toEqual({ auth: AUTH_URL, mail: { smtpUrl: MAIL.SMTP_URL, mailFrom: MAIL.MAIL_FROM, requireTls: false } });
    expect(revokeSettings({ DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, ...MAIL, NODE_ENV: "production" }).mail.requireTls).toBe(true);
  });

  test("a setting only the API reads, or one the API's configuration would refuse, changes nothing", () => {
    const env = { DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, ...MAIL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "https://console.example/", APP_ORIGIN: "not a url", AUTH_HMAC_KEY: "c2hvcnQ=", DATABASE_URL_API: "nope" };
    expect(revokeSettings(env).auth).toBe(AUTH_URL);
  });

  test("names the setting that is missing or wrong, and no other", () => {
    const cases: [Record<string, string>, RegExp][] = [
      [{ ...MAIL }, /DATABASE_URL_AUTH/],
      [{ DATABASE_URL_AUTH: "mysql://x@localhost/k", ...MAIL }, /DATABASE_URL_AUTH/],
      [{ DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, MAIL_FROM: MAIL.MAIL_FROM }, /SMTP_URL/],
      [{ DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, SMTP_URL: "http://localhost:1025", MAIL_FROM: MAIL.MAIL_FROM }, /SMTP_URL/],
      [{ DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, SMTP_URL: MAIL.SMTP_URL }, /MAIL_FROM/],
    ];
    for (const [env, named] of cases) {
      let message = "";
      try {
        revokeSettings(env);
      } catch (err) {
        message = (err as Error).message;
      }
      expect(message, JSON.stringify(env)).toMatch(named);
      expect(message).toMatch(/^Invalid environment for revoke:/);
      expect(message).not.toMatch(/APP_ORIGIN|REDIS_URL|AUTH_HMAC_KEY|CONSOLE_ORIGIN|DATABASE_URL_API|DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE/);
    }
  });

  test("run with a setting missing, it names it, answers 1 and connects to nothing", async () => {
    const { lines, out } = capture();
    const started = Date.now();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["revoke", "mod@korbat.local", "all"], { DATABASE_URL_AUTH: "postgres://korbat_auth:x@127.0.0.1:1/korbat", ...MAIL, SMTP_URL: "" }, out)).toBe(1);
    expect(Date.now() - started).toBeLessThan(2_000);
    expect(lines).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(lines[0]).toMatch(/^err Invalid environment for revoke:/);
    expect(lines[0]).toContain("SMTP_URL");
  });
});

describe("staff.js: the commands for moderation cases (3c design, section 7.13)", () => {
  const CASE = "3f1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a";
  const MIGRATE_URL = "postgres://korbat_migrate:x@localhost:5432/korbat";

  test("the usage lists them, and says which run in the migrate service", () => {
    for (const words of ["text-verify", "access-request <@handle | email>", "link <staff email> <personal handle>", "unlink <staff email> <personal handle>", "limits <decisions per hour> <decisions per day> <case opens per day> <findings per day> <reveals per day>"]) {
      expect(STAFF_USAGE, words).toContain(words);
    }
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("linked to it");
    // 3f Task 5: notification-facts replaces account-facts, and the record commands are listed with the order commands.
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).not.toContain("account-facts");
    for (const words of ["records [--verify]", "notification-facts <record>", "notification-sent <record>", "production-account <order>", "address-check --handle <handle> < address", "handover-list <seal action>", "handover-record <production>", "handover-destroyed <production>"]) {
      expect(STAFF_USAGE, words).toContain(`  ${words}`);
    }
  });

  test("reads link and unlink with a staff address and a personal handle, with or without its at sign, in lower case", () => {
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["link", " Mod@Korbat.Local ", "@Ada_L"])).toEqual({ command: "link", email: "mod@korbat.local", handle: "ada_l" });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["unlink", "mod@korbat.local", "ada_l"])).toEqual({ command: "unlink", email: "mod@korbat.local", handle: "ada_l" });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["link", "mod@korbat.local"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["link", "mod@korbat.local", "ada", "bob"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["link", "moderator", "ada"])).toThrow(`not an email address: moderator\n${STAFF_USAGE}`);
    for (const handle of ["ada lovelace", "ada@korbat.local", "@", "a-b", "'; drop table profiles; --"]) {
      expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["unlink", "mod@korbat.local", handle]), handle).toThrow(`not a handle: ${handle}`);
    }
  });

  test("reads limits with exactly five whole numbers from 1, in the order of the usage", () => {
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["limits", "60", "300", "400", "50", "10"])).toEqual({
      command: "limits",
      limits: { decisionsPerHour: 60, decisionsPerDay: 300, caseOpensPerDay: 400, findingsPerDay: 50, revealsPerDay: 10 },
    });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["limits", "60", "300", "400", "50"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["limits", "60", "300", "400", "50", "10", "5"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    for (const number of ["0", "-1", "1.5", "1e3", "ten", "", " 5", "05", "12345678"]) {
      expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["limits", "60", "300", number, "50", "10"]), JSON.stringify(number)).toThrow(`not a limit: ${number}`);
    }
  });

  test("reads text-verify without arguments, the record commands with what they name and their flags, and access-request with a handle or an address", () => {
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["text-verify"])).toEqual({ command: "text-verify" });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["text-verify", "now"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    // 3f Task 5: account-facts is gone; notification-facts names a record.
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["account-facts", "@Ada", CASE])).toThrow("unknown command: account-facts");
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["notification-facts", CASE])).toEqual({ command: "record", record: { command: "notification-facts", target: CASE, positional: [], flags: new Map() } });
    const sent = parseStaffArgs(["notification-sent", CASE, "--duty", "dsa18_1", "--duty", "tco14_5", "--kinds", "handle,address"]);
    expect(sent).toMatchObject({ command: "record", record: { command: "notification-sent", target: CASE } });
    expect((sent as { record: { flags: Map<string, string[]> } }).record.flags.get("--duty")).toEqual(["dsa18_1", "tco14_5"]);
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["records", "--verify"])).toMatchObject({ command: "record", record: { command: "records", target: null } });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["records", CASE])).toThrow(/records: takes no/);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["notification-facts"])).toThrow(/notification-facts: name the record/);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["handover-list", "--instrument"])).toThrow(/needs a value/);
    // An at sign in front is a handle's; one inside is an address's.
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["access-request", "@Ada"])).toEqual({ command: "access-request", who: { handle: "ada" } });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["access-request", "ada"])).toEqual({ command: "access-request", who: { handle: "ada" } });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["access-request", " Ada@Korbat.Local "])).toEqual({ command: "access-request", who: { email: "ada@korbat.local" } });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["access-request"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["access-request", "ada", "bob"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["access-request", "ada lovelace"])).toThrow("not a handle: ada lovelace");
  });

  test("text-verify reads DATABASE_URL_API alone; link, unlink and limits the migrator's URL alone", () => {
    expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "text-verify" }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL })).toEqual({ api: API_URL, auth: null });
    expect(() => staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "text-verify" }, { DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL })).toThrow(/DATABASE_URL_API/);
    expect(migratorUrl("limits", { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "not an origin", SMTP_URL: "nonsense" })).toBe(MIGRATE_URL);
    expect(() => migratorUrl("link", { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL })).toThrow(/Invalid environment for link:[^]*DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE/);
  });

  test("run in the wrong service, each says which URL it lacks, answers 1 and connects to nothing", async () => {
    for (const args of [["link", "mod@korbat.local", "ada"], ["unlink", "mod@korbat.local", "ada"], ["limits", "60", "300", "400", "50", "10"], ["records"], ["notification-facts", CASE]]) {
      const { lines, out } = capture();
      expect(await runStaffCommand(args, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL }, out), args[0]).toBe(1);
      expect(lines, args[0]).toHaveLength(1);
      expect(lines[0], args[0]).toMatch(new RegExp(`^err Invalid environment for ${args[0]}:`));
      expect(lines[0], args[0]).toContain("DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE");
    }
    // access-request for an address reads the API's whole configuration, and refuses with what is missing of it.
    const { lines, out } = capture();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["access-request", "ada@korbat.local"], { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL }, out)).toBe(1);
    expect(lines).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(lines[0]).toMatch(/^err /);
    expect(lines[0]).toContain("DATABASE_URL_API");
    // 3f Task 5: for a handle it runs in the migrate service, which holds the migrator's URL and APP_ORIGIN.
    const handle = capture();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["access-request", "@ada"], { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL }, handle.out)).toBe(1);
    expect(handle.lines).toEqual(["err access-request: a handle's draft runs in the migrate service, which holds DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE and APP_ORIGIN; nothing was drafted"]);
    const noOrigin = capture();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["access-request", "@ada"], { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL }, noOrigin.out)).toBe(1);
    expect(noOrigin.lines).toEqual(handle.lines);
  });
});

describe("staff.js tco-counts (3f design, section 8.11, Recovery and the counts)", () => {
  const MIGRATE_URL = "postgres://korbat_migrate:x@localhost:5432/korbat";

  test("the usage lists it with its first line, in the migrate service", () => {
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("  tco-counts <year>");
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toMatch(/tco-counts <year> +print the figures of TCO Art\. 7\(3\) and 21\(1\) for that calendar year in UTC/);
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("read-only; run it in the migrate service");
  });

  test("reads a year of four digits and nothing else", () => {
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["tco-counts", "2025"])).toEqual({ command: "counts", counts: { command: "tco-counts", year: 2025 } });
    for (const args of [["tco-counts"], ["tco-counts", "25"], ["tco-counts", "2025", "2026"], ["tco-counts", "20x5"], ["tco-counts", "02025"], ["tco-counts", "--year", "2025"]]) {
      expect(() => parseStaffArgs(args), args.join(" ")).toThrow(/^tco-counts: /);
    }
  });

  test("reads the migrator's URL alone: run in the api service it says so, answers 1 and connects to nothing", async () => {
    expect(migratorUrl("tco-counts", { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, DATABASE_URL_API: "nonsense" })).toBe(MIGRATE_URL);
    const { lines, out } = capture();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["tco-counts", "2025"], { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL }, out)).toBe(1);
    expect(lines).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(lines[0]).toMatch(/^err Invalid environment for tco-counts:/);
    expect(lines[0]).toContain("DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE");
  });
});
