        "Report what you believe breaks a rule; a report that turns out wrong costs you nothing.",
        "korbat acts only on reports that are manifestly unfounded",
        "You see the mark on your list of reports together with the report's outcome, and you can ask for a re-examination.",
        "a report counts once, by the day you sent it, however many of its items were marked, so no single report can lead to a warning.",
        "the count alone decides nothing",
        "Notices of illegal content, reports of child sexual abuse material and requests for re-examination are never counted and never restricted.",
        "You can appeal the warning and the restriction.",
      ],
      Handles: [
        "When the breach lies in a handle itself (impersonation, someone's private information, a threat), a moderator may retire it.",
        "A retired handle can be used by nobody again, you included.",
        "you can choose a new handle without the usual wait: at once, or, while your account is suspended, when the suspension ends.",
        "nobody else could take it meanwhile",
        "also when the breach was someone's private information (rule R4): refusing it needs it.",
      ],
      Appeals: [
        "If a final decision restricts your content or your account, you can appeal it once",
        "An appeal never holds the start of a suspension; a reply does.",
        "The appeal of a protective suspension is reviewed at once; only the appeal of a decision that seals images waits for the authorities.",
      ],
      "Reports and notices": [
        "When korbat's answer to a report about an account is a measure on that account, korbat tells you that it took a measure, and not which or for how long",
        "korbat does not tell you what happens to that account afterwards.",
      ],
      "Your data": [
        "korbat keeps the record of every strike, suspension, termination, warning and retired handle with its decision, as it keeps every decision. What ends is its use:",
        "To decide about reporting in bad faith korbat counts, for each account and day, how many reports under its rules the account sent, and keeps which of them a moderator marked manifestly unfounded;",
        "so for that long a marked report stays linked to the account that sent it. A retired handle is kept as a handle (Handles). Your export holds all of this.",
        "while it can still be re-examined, except through the mark of a report found manifestly unfounded (Reporting in bad faith).",
      ],
    };
    for (const [title, sentences] of Object.entries(said)) for (const sentence of sentences) expect(bodyOf(terms, title), `${title}: ${sentence}`).toContain(sentence);
    // No text says more of a mail than korbat knows: it was sent, never delivered or handed over.
    const all = terms.TERMS_SECTIONS.map((section) => section.body).join(" ");
    expect(all).not.toMatch(/delivered|handed to your mail provider/);
    // A protective suspension is never worded as a finding.
    expect(bodyOf(terms, "Suspension and termination")).not.toContain("It breaks");
  });
});

describe("3f's sections and sentences (design, W.6)", () => {
  test("Authorities' orders holds the design's four paragraphs", () => {
    expect(paragraphsOf(terms, "Authorities' orders")).toEqual([
      "An authority or a court of the European Union or of one of its countries can order korbat to act against a post, or to give information about an account. korbat carries such an order out within the time the law sets and checks that it comes from the authority it names; if it does not, korbat reinstates the post and tells you. A removal order for terrorist content leaves korbat no choice, and has to be carried out within one hour, so korbat may act on it before that check is finished. Any other order korbat checks first, and carries out because the law under which it was issued requires it. korbat does not assess the post under its own rules when it carries out an order: such an order is not a decision of korbat's.",
      "So korbat gives no reasons of its own for it, and korbat's appeal does not apply. You get a notice instead, under Settings, Cases, announced by an email that says only that there is one. The notice says which authority the order names, under which law, on which day and under which reference, and whether korbat has confirmed that it comes from that authority. It gives the authority's reasons and the ways to challenge the order, in the authority's own words, as soon as korbat has them; when korbat adds them later it sends you an email, and the notice says since when it has held them. The notice also says how to ask korbat for a copy of the order.",
      "An order can forbid korbat to tell you about it for a time. Then korbat keeps the post from you as from everyone, tells you nothing, and can say nothing about the post by email either. For a removal order the law sets that time (Terrorist content); for another order the authority that issued it does, and korbat tells you when that authority allows. While korbat may not tell you of an order, it cannot tell you of a decision it takes about the same post under its own rules, or answer an appeal you made about that post before: you get those together with the notice.",
      "korbat lifts what it did only when the authority withdraws the order, when a court annuls it, when the authority of korbat's own country finds that an order from another country infringes the law, when the order turns out not to be authentic, or when korbat disabled a post that the order did not name. For that last case write to the address under Contact, from the email address of your account. When korbat's own rules apply to the same post, that is a second decision, with its own statement of reasons and its own appeal. korbat cannot act for one country alone, so an order takes effect everywhere korbat is available.",
    ]);
  });

  test("Contact point for authorities prints the build's address; the languages are left out while the state's entry declares none", () => {
    expect(terms.CONTACT_POINT).toBe(CONTACT_POINT);
    expect(contracts.STATE_FACTS.DE!.languages).toBeNull();
    expect(paragraphsOf(terms, "Contact point for authorities")).toEqual([
      `Authorities of the Member States, the European Commission and the European Board for Digital Services reach korbat at ${CONTACT_POINT} (Article 11 of the Digital Services Act; Article 15 of Regulation (EU) 2021/784). This address is for authorities. Everyone else writes to the address under Contact, and reports content with the report form.`,
    ]);
  });

  test("Who can use korbat names the build's Member State by its name in STATE_FACTS; What you can post points to Authorities' orders", () => {
    expect(bodyOf(terms, "Who can use korbat")).toBe(
      "You must be at least 16 years old. You can use a pseudonym. One person may hold more than one account, but not to carry on what another of their accounts was suspended or terminated for (Suspension and termination). korbat is established in Germany and offers its service there only.",
    );
    expect(bodyOf(terms, "What you can post")).toContain("The one restriction that is not korbat's decision is an authority's order (Authorities' orders).");
  });

  test("Appeals says that korbat's appeal does not apply to an order, and when a held answer and a held decision's appeal count from", () => {
    const appeals = paragraphsOf(terms, "Appeals");
    const at = appeals.indexOf(
      "korbat's appeal does not apply to what korbat does on an authority's order. If such an order forbids korbat to tell you about a post, korbat's answer to an appeal you made about that post reaches you only when it may tell you of the order; your time to appeal a decision you are told of late counts from the day you are told.",
    );
    expect(at).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    // Before the courts, which stay the section's last word.
    expect(at).toBe(appeals.length - 2);
  });

  test("Your data gains the four paragraphs and the periods of what concerns authorities, before the export's paragraph", () => {
    const data = paragraphsOf(terms, "Your data");
    const added = [
      "Two things the law can oblige korbat to keep for a time when you delete your account; everything else is deleted at once. First, your email address: when korbat has sealed images of your account, the law may oblige it to report them to the authorities. Until it has done so, or has decided that it need not, and for seven days at most, korbat keeps the address, and nothing else of the account; it uses it for that report alone, and the email that confirms your deletion tells you. You can write to korbat about this at the address under Contact, complain to a data protection authority, and go to court. Second, a post that an authority's order obliges korbat to preserve: korbat keeps it, with its images, until that time ends (Terrorist content), also after your account is gone.",
      "korbat keeps a record of every report it makes to an authority and of everything it hands to one: which duty, which authority, when, both references, what was asked for and which kinds of data, never a copy of the data. It keeps these records and its records of authorities' orders for three years after the matter's last event, an order's record for as long as its measure stands, and a record that says you may not be told of something for as long as that holds. korbat records when a message reaches its contact point for authorities, never who sent it or what it says, and deletes that record 30 days after the message was handled.",
      "When an authority lawfully asks who holds an account, korbat gives the handle, the email address and the day the account was created. korbat also holds when and from which kind of device an account signed in; it gives those only when an order names them and the law requires it, and its record says so. korbat tells you when it has given an authority information about your account, with the authority's reasons and the ways to challenge its order, unless the order, or the law under which it was issued, forbids telling you or delays it; korbat records which of these applies and on what basis. While korbat may not tell you, its answer to a data request of yours leaves the matter out, and korbat keeps the reason on record.",
      "If korbat has to restore its database from a backup, it may have to take a decision about you again; the decision then says so.",
      "The periods for what concerns authorities: content disabled under a removal order is kept six months and one day from the disabling, and from the new disabling when it was reinstated and disabled again, longer on an authority's or a court's request, and is then erased. An order's records, and the records of a notification or a production, are kept three years after the matter's last event; an order's never while its measure stands, and a record of an authority's demand that a person is not told never while that demand holds. The record of a message at the contact point for authorities is kept 30 days, counted from the day the message was handled; the record of a message nobody handled is kept until a person has closed it. A gap a restore left is kept 12 months when it was closed as not needed or imported; a gap that a decision taken again closed is kept as long as that decision. The email address of a deleted account is kept while a report is owed, seven days at most.",
    ];
    const at = data.indexOf(added[0]!);
    expect(at).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(data.slice(at, at + added.length)).toEqual(added);
    expect(data[at + added.length]).toMatch(/^Your account's export holds/);
  });

  describe("with other values of the build's two arguments and of STATE_FACTS", () => {
    /** The terms module as a build with these arguments, and these facts of the states, makes it. */
    async function built(env: { point?: string; state?: string }, facts?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<TermsModule> {
      const saved = { point: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT, state: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE };
      vi.resetModules();
      if (env.point === undefined) delete process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT;
      else process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT = env.point;
      if (env.state === undefined) delete process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE;
      else process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE = env.state;
      if (facts) vi.doMock("@korbat/contracts", async (importOriginal) => ({ ...(await importOriginal<Contracts>()), STATE_FACTS: facts }));
      try {
        return await import("../src/lib/terms");
      } finally {
        vi.doUnmock("@korbat/contracts");
        process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT = saved.point;
        process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE = saved.state;
      }
    }

    test("without them the terms print no contact point and name no state, and every other section stands", async () => {
      const bare = await built({});
      const titles = bare.TERMS_SECTIONS.map((section) => section.title);
      expect(titles).not.toContain("Contact point for authorities");
      expect(titles).toEqual(terms.TERMS_SECTIONS.map((section) => section.title).filter((title) => title !== "Contact point for authorities"));
      expect(bodyOf(bare, "Who can use korbat")).not.toContain("korbat is established in");
      expect(bare.CONTACT_POINT).toBe("");
    });

    test("with the state's languages declared, the contact point names them; a state the contracts do not fill in is named by its code", async () => {
      const declared = await built({ point: CONTACT_POINT, state: "DE" }, { DE: { ...contracts.STATE_FACTS.DE!, languages: ["English", "German"] } });
      expect(bodyOf(declared, "Contact point for authorities")).toContain(`reach korbat at ${CONTACT_POINT} (Article 11 of the Digital Services Act; Article 15 of Regulation (EU) 2021/784), in English and German. This address is for authorities.`);
      const unknown = await built({ point: CONTACT_POINT, state: "AT" });
      expect(bodyOf(unknown, "Who can use korbat")).toContain("korbat is established in AT and offers its service there only.");
      expect(bodyOf(unknown, "Contact point for authorities")).toContain(`(Article 11 of the Digital Services Act; Article 15 of Regulation (EU) 2021/784). This address`);
    });
  });
});

describe("the table tests: the terms' numbers, rules, measures and outcomes are their constants'", () => {
  test("the table of numbers names every number of NOTICE_LIMITS, CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS, SUSPECT_EARLIER_MONTHS, APPEAL_MONTHS, DAILY_LIMITS, RETENTION, STANDING_RULES and REPLY_AIM_HOURS, and the two of ORDER_RULES the terms print", () => {
    expect([...new Set(numbersTable(contracts).map((row) => row.constant))].sort()).toEqual(constantPaths(contracts).sort());
  });

  test("the terms print every one of them in its sentence, every rule with its text, every measure's label in the sentence its marks put it in, and every outcome's phrase with what it means", () => {
    holds(terms, contracts, rules);
    // As they stand today, in the words a reader meets.
    const text = moderationText(terms);
    expect(text["Reports and notices"]).toContain("korbat takes at most 5 reports an hour and 20 a day from one network without an account, and 10 an hour and 50 a day from one account.");
    expect(text["Reports and notices"]).toContain("one report can name one profile at most");
    expect(text["Appeals"]).toContain("within six months of being told");
    expect(text["Your data"]).toContain("Each is deleted 30 days after it was taken");
    expect(text["How moderators decide"]).toContain("under R2 or R5 or on a report made on the anonymous path");
    expect(labelsIn(measuresSentence(terms, LEADS.interim))).toEqual(["Withhold the post", "Withhold one image"]);
    expect(labelsIn(measuresSentence(terms, LEADS.final))).toEqual(["Remove", "Remove one image", "Strike", "Suspend the account", "Terminate the account", "Retire the handle", "Warn about reporting", "Restrict reporting"]);
    expect(labelsIn(measuresSentence(terms, LEADS.either))).toEqual(["Seal the images this case reaches", "Reset display name", "Reset bio"]);
    expect(text["Reports and notices"]).toContain('"access restricted: it breaks korbat rule [number] ([title])": ');
    // 3e's numbers as a reader meets them.
    expect(text["Strikes"]).toContain("It counts for 90 days from its decision.");
    expect(text["Suspension and termination"]).toContain("for at most three days the first time, seven the second and 30 the third, counting the suspensions decided in the last 365 days");
    expect(text["Suspension and termination"]).toContain("The suspension starts 168 hours after korbat sent that email. If korbat's mail service refuses your address or cannot send the email for five days, only the app can tell you, and the suspension starts 336 hours after the decision.");
    expect(text["Suspension and termination"]).toContain("it made 20 or more posts within 60 minutes, for up to seven days");
    expect(text["Suspension and termination"]).toContain("korbat aims to answer a reply to a suspension taken at once within 24 hours.");
    expect(text["Reporting in bad faith"]).toContain("If at least five of the reports you sent under the rules within 90 days are marked, and they are at least half of the reports you sent under the rules in that time");
    expect(text["Handles"]).toContain("a placeholder that begins with retired_,");
    expect(text["Your data"]).toContain("a strike counts for 90 days, a suspension counts toward the next one for 365 days, a warning about reporting for 90 days.");
    // 3f's numbers as a reader meets them.
    expect(text["Terrorist content"]).toContain("korbat keeps it, with its images and a copy of its text, for six months from the disabling");
    expect(text["Your data"]).toContain("and for seven days at most, korbat keeps the address");
    expect(text["Your data"]).toContain("A gap a restore left is kept 12 months when it was closed as not needed or imported");
  });

  test("the terms name no measure the constants lack and no ban; every kind of the ledger is quoted; and no number but the constants', the emergency switch's 48 hours and the Regulation's own", () => {
    const text = moderationText(terms);
    const all = Object.values(text).join(" ");
    // 3e names strikes, suspensions and retired handles (W.7), 3f an order's preservation (W.6); korbat bans nobody.
    expect(all).toMatch(/preserv/i);
    for (const absent of [/\bban(s|ned)?\b/i]) expect(absent.test(all), String(absent)).toBe(false);
    // The quoted labels are the ledger's 24 kinds (3f adds the order's measure and its reversal) and nothing else.
    const labels = Object.values(LEADS).flatMap((lead) => labelsIn(measuresSentence(terms, lead)));
    expect([...labels].sort()).toEqual(contracts.ACTION_KINDS.map((kind) => contracts.MEASURES[kind].label).sort());
    // Every run of digits outside the rulebook's own texts, a rule's number and the Regulation's articles is a constant's.
    const values = new Set<string>();
    const collect = (value: unknown): void => {
      if (typeof value === "number") values.add(String(value));
      else if (value !== null && typeof value === "object") Object.values(value).forEach(collect);
    };
    collect([contracts.NOTICE_LIMITS, contracts.DAILY_LIMITS, contracts.RETENTION, contracts.CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS, contracts.SUSPECT_EARLIER_MONTHS, contracts.APPEAL_MONTHS, contracts.STANDING_RULES, contracts.REPLY_AIM_HOURS]);
    collect([contracts.ORDER_RULES.reportHoldDays, contracts.ORDER_RULES.preserveMarginDays]);
    const outside = Object.entries(text)
      .filter(([title]) => title !== "The rules")
      .map(([, body]) => body)
      .join(" ")
      .replace(/Article [0-9]+ of /g, " ")
      .replace(/Article [0-9]+\([0-9]+\)|Regulation \(EU\) [0-9]+\/[0-9]+/g, " ")
      .replace(/\bR[1-6]\b/g, " ");
    const typed = (outside.match(/[0-9]+/g) ?? []).filter((digits) => !values.has(digits));
    // The age of an account under the emergency switch has no constant: the queue's own query holds the same 48 hours.
    // 3f: and the scrutiny's 48 hours, TCO Art. 4(4)'s own period.
    expect(typed).toEqual(["48", "48"]);
    expect(text["Reports and notices"]).toContain("from accounts under 48 hours old");
    expect(text["Terrorist content"]).toContain("within 48 hours of receiving its reasons");
  });

  describe("with other numbers, another rulebook, other labels and other phrases in the constants", () => {
    let changed: { terms: TermsModule; contracts: Contracts; rules: Rules };

    beforeAll(async () => {
      vi.resetModules();
      // Every number of the constants becomes another, each its own and none a number the terms print today.
      let next = 100;
      const renumber = (value: unknown): unknown => {
        if (typeof value === "number") return ++next;
        if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(renumber);
        if (value === null || typeof value !== "object") return value;
        return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(value).map(([key, member]) => [key, renumber(member)]));
      };
      vi.doMock("@korbat/contracts", async (importOriginal) => {
        const actual = await importOriginal<Contracts>();
        return {
          ...actual,
          NOTICE_LIMITS: renumber(actual.NOTICE_LIMITS),
          DAILY_LIMITS: renumber(actual.DAILY_LIMITS),
          // RETENTION's one phrase is changed too, as a rule's text is.
          RETENTION: { ...(renumber(actual.RETENTION) as object), replyText: "for the period of a reply's text" },
          STANDING_RULES: renumber(actual.STANDING_RULES),
          REPLY_AIM_HOURS: renumber(actual.REPLY_AIM_HOURS),
          // 3f: the two numbers of ORDER_RULES the terms print by themselves (the others through RETENTION).
          ORDER_RULES: renumber(actual.ORDER_RULES),
          ACCOUNT_MEASURE_SCOPE: { retired: "the phrase of a retirement.", measure: "the phrase of an account measure." },
          RETIRED_HANDLE_PREFIX: "gone_",
          APPEAL_MONTHS: renumber(actual.APPEAL_MONTHS),
          CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS: renumber(actual.CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS),
          SUSPECT_EARLIER_MONTHS: renumber(actual.SUSPECT_EARLIER_MONTHS),
          // Other labels, and a removal that may also be taken while deciding: it moves to the third sentence.
          MEASURES: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(actual.MEASURES).map(([kind, spec]) => [kind, { ...spec, label: `the label of ${kind}`, ...(kind === "remove" ? { interim: true } : {}) }])),
          OUTCOME_PHRASES: Object.fromEntries(actual.ITEM_OUTCOMES.map((outcome) => [outcome, outcome === "restricted_rule" ? "the phrase of restricted_rule {rule} ({title})" : `the phrase of ${outcome}`])),
          SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES: { sealed: "the phrase of a seal.", no_action: "the phrase of no action on that path." },
          UNSEEN_NO_ACTION: "the phrase of an answer given unseen.",
        };
      });
      vi.doMock("@korbat/rules", async (importOriginal) => {
        const actual = await importOriginal<Rules>();
        return {
          ...actual,
          RULES_VERSION: 9,
          // Other titles and texts, and a third rule that only an admin decides.
          RULES: actual.RULES.map((rule) => ({ ...rule, title: `No title of ${rule.id}`, text: `The text of ${rule.id}.`, seniorQueue: rule.seniorQueue || rule.id === "R3" })),
        };
      });
      changed = { terms: await import("../src/lib/terms"), contracts: await import("@korbat/contracts"), rules: await import("@korbat/rules") };
      vi.doUnmock("@korbat/contracts");
      vi.doUnmock("@korbat/rules");
    });

    test("the constants the terms were built from are the changed ones", () => {
      expect(changed.contracts.RETENTION.backupDays).not.toBe(contracts.RETENTION.backupDays);
      expect(changed.contracts.STANDING_RULES.strikeDays).not.toBe(contracts.STANDING_RULES.strikeDays);
      expect(changed.contracts.STANDING_RULES.ladderDays).toHaveLength(3);
      expect(changed.contracts.APPEAL_MONTHS).toBeGreaterThan(100);
      expect(changed.contracts.ORDER_RULES.reportHoldDays).toBeGreaterThan(100);
      expect(changed.rules.RULES_VERSION).toBe(9);
      expect(changed.terms).not.toBe(terms);
    });

    test("the terms print the changed numbers, rulebook, labels and phrases, each in its place", () => {
      holds(changed.terms, changed.contracts, changed.rules);
      const text = moderationText(changed.terms);
      expect(text["How moderators decide"]).toContain("under R2, R3 or R5 or on a report made on the anonymous path");
      expect(labelsIn(measuresSentence(changed.terms, LEADS.final))).toEqual(["remove_media", "strike", "suspend", "terminate", "retire_handle", "warn_reporting", "restrict_reporting"].map((kind) => `the label of ${kind}`));
      expect(labelsIn(measuresSentence(changed.terms, LEADS.either))).toEqual(["the label of remove", "the label of seal_media", "the label of reset_display_name", "the label of reset_bio"]);
      expect(text["What you can post"]).toContain("(title of R1, title of R2, title of R3, title of R4, title of R5, title of R6)");
    });

    test("and not one of today's: no number, rule title, rule text, label or phrase is typed into the terms", () => {
      const text = moderationText(changed.terms);
      const all = Object.values(text).join(" ");
      for (const row of numbersTable(contracts)) expect(text[row.section]!.includes(row.phrase), `${row.constant}: "${row.phrase}"`).toBe(false);
      for (const rule of rules.RULES) {
        expect(all.includes(rule.text), rule.id).toBe(false);
        expect(all.includes(rule.title), rule.id).toBe(false);
        // A rule's name is also a common word in these sections ("child sexual abuse material"), so it is looked for
        // where the terms list the rules by name, and in brackets, as a sentence names the rule on doxxing.
        expect(text["What you can post"]!.includes(ruleName(rule)), rule.id).toBe(false);
        expect(all.includes(`(${ruleName(rule)})`), rule.id).toBe(false);
      }
      for (const spec of Object.values(contracts.MEASURES)) expect(all.includes(`"${spec.label}"`), spec.label).toBe(false);
      for (const phrase of outcomePhrases(contracts)) expect(all.includes(quoted(phrase)), phrase).toBe(false);
      // 3e: the scope phrases, the placeholder's prefix and a reply's period are the constants', never typed.
      for (const phrase of [contracts.ACCOUNT_MEASURE_SCOPE.measure, contracts.ACCOUNT_MEASURE_SCOPE.retired, contracts.RETIRED_HANDLE_PREFIX, contracts.RETENTION.replyText]) expect(all.includes(phrase), phrase).toBe(false);
      // The only digits left that no changed constant printed are the emergency switch's and the Regulation's.
      const values = new Set<string>();
      const collect = (value: unknown): void => {
        if (typeof value === "number") values.add(String(value));
        else if (value !== null && typeof value === "object") Object.values(value).forEach(collect);
      };
      const c = changed.contracts;
      // 3e prints two numbers worked out from a constant: the earlier strikes after a suspension, and the share as a percentage.
      collect([c.NOTICE_LIMITS, c.DAILY_LIMITS, c.RETENTION, c.CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS, c.SUSPECT_EARLIER_MONTHS, c.APPEAL_MONTHS, c.APPEAL_MONTHS + Math.ceil(c.RETENTION.intakeDays / 30), changed.rules.RULES_VERSION]);
      collect([c.STANDING_RULES, c.REPLY_AIM_HOURS, c.STANDING_RULES.ladderStrikes - 1, c.STANDING_RULES.reportWarnShare * 100]);
      collect([c.ORDER_RULES.reportHoldDays, c.ORDER_RULES.preserveMarginDays]);
      const outside = all.replace(/Article [0-9]+ of /g, " ").replace(/Article [0-9]+\([0-9]+\)|Regulation \(EU\) [0-9]+\/[0-9]+/g, " ").replace(/\bR[1-6]\b/g, " ");
      expect((outside.match(/[0-9]+/g) ?? []).filter((digits) => !values.has(digits))).toEqual(["48", "48"]);
    });
  });
});

describe("the terms page", () => {
  test("shows every section under its heading and every paragraph of it, then Contact with the build's address and the link to the report form", () => {
    const out = html(<Terms />);
    const text = textOf(out);
    expect(text).toContain(`Version ${terms.TERMS_VERSION}`);
    let at = 0;
    for (const section of terms.TERMS_SECTIONS) {
      // Each heading after the one before it, with its paragraphs behind it in order.
      // A title's apostrophe is written as the markup escapes it (3f: "Authorities' orders").
      const heading = out.indexOf(`>${section.title.replaceAll("'", "&#x27;")}</`, at);
      expect(heading, section.title).toBeGreaterThan(at);
      at = heading;
      let within = textOf(out.slice(heading));
      for (const paragraph of terms.termsParagraphs(section.body)) {
        const found = within.indexOf(textOf(paragraph));
        expect(found, `${section.title}: ${paragraph.slice(0, 60)}`).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
        within = within.slice(found);
      }
    }
    // One level-2 heading for each section, and one for Contact.
    expect(out.split("<h2").length - 1).toBe(terms.TERMS_SECTIONS.length + 1);
    // Every paragraph is an element of its own: a reader gets them apart, not as one block. Its first words stand
    // directly behind an opening tag's end.
    const decoded = out.replaceAll("&#x27;", "'").replaceAll("&quot;", '"').replaceAll("&gt;", ">");
    for (const paragraph of terms.TERMS_SECTIONS.flatMap((section) => terms.termsParagraphs(section.body))) {
      const start = paragraph.slice(0, 40);
      expect(decoded.includes(`>${start}`), start).toBe(true);
    }
    expect(text).toContain(`Contact ${CONTACT_WORDS.body(CONTACT)}`);
    expect(text.indexOf("Your account's export holds")).toBeLessThan(text.indexOf("Contact Write to korbat"));
    expect(text.indexOf("Contact Write to korbat")).toBeLessThan(text.indexOf(CONTACT_WORDS.report));
    expect(out).toContain('href="/report"');
  });
});

describe("the web build's two arguments for the terms (3f, Task 7): the contact point for authorities and the home state", () => {
  const REPO = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..", "..", "..");
  const repo = (...parts: string[]) => readFileSync(path.join(REPO, ...parts), "utf8");

  test("the terms read both from the build, and both example files carry the development values: no contact point, the API's state", () => {
    const source = repo("apps", "app", "src", "lib", "terms.ts");
    expect(source).toContain('export const CONTACT_POINT = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT ?? "";');
    expect(source).toContain('export const HOME_STATE = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE ?? "";');
    const infra = repo("infra", ".env.example");
    expect(infra).toMatch(/^WEB_CONTACT_POINT=$/m);
    expect(infra).toMatch(/^WEB_HOME_STATE=DE$/m);
    // The same two values the API holds, which the build cannot read.
    expect(infra).toMatch(/^API_CONTACT_POINT=$/m);
    expect(infra).toMatch(/^API_HOME_STATE=DE$/m);
    const app = repo("apps", "app", ".env.example");
    expect(app).toMatch(/^EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT=$/m);
    expect(app).toMatch(/^EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE=DE$/m);
  });

  test("the compose service passes both, neither required; the web image checks each when set and passes both to the export", () => {
    const compose = repo("infra", "compose.yml");
    expect(compose).toContain("EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT: ${WEB_CONTACT_POINT:-}");
    expect(compose).toContain("EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE: ${WEB_HOME_STATE:-}");
    const dockerfile = repo("infra", "caddy", "Dockerfile");
    for (const line of [
      "ARG EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT=",
      "ARG EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE=",
      'RUN case "$EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT" in "") ;; *?@?*.?*) ;; *) echo "the EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT build argument must be empty or an email address" >&2; exit 1;; esac',
      `RUN case "$EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE" in "") ;; [A-Z][A-Z]) ;; *) echo "the EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE build argument must be empty or a Member State's two-letter code" >&2; exit 1;; esac`,
      'RUN if [ -n "$EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT" ] && [ -z "$EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE" ]; then echo "EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT needs EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE: the terms name the state whose authorities write to it" >&2; exit 1; fi',
      'RUN if [ "$KORBAT_ENV" = "production" ] && [ -n "$EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT" ]; then case "$(printf %s "${EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT##*@}" | tr A-Z a-z)" in *.local|*.localhost|*.test|*.invalid|*.example|example.com|example.org|example.net) echo "EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT is a placeholder address; a production build needs the address authorities write to" >&2; exit 1;; esac; fi',
      'EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT="$EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT" EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE="$EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE" npx expo export --platform web',
    ]) {
      expect(dockerfile, line).toContain(line);
      // Each check after KORBAT_ENV is declared and before the export.
      expect(dockerfile.indexOf("ARG KORBAT_ENV"), line).toBeLessThan(dockerfile.indexOf(line));
    }
    expect(dockerfile.indexOf("needs EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE")).toBeLessThan(dockerfile.indexOf("npx expo export"));
  });
});

describe("the order of a decision's actions", () => {
  const a = "1a1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a";
  const b = "2a1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a";

    const sorted: DecisionActionParams[] = [
      { kind: "remove", mediaId: null },
      { kind: "remove_media", mediaId: a },
      { kind: "remove_media", mediaId: b },
      { kind: "reset_bio", mediaId: null },
      { kind: "seal_media", mediaId: null },
      { kind: "withhold_media", mediaId: a },
    ];
    for (const shuffled of [[...sorted].reverse(), [sorted[3]!, sorted[0]!, sorted[5]!, sorted[2]!, sorted[1]!, sorted[4]!]]) {
      expect([...shuffled].sort(compareDecisionActions)).toEqual(sorted);
    }
    expect(compareDecisionActions(sorted[1]!, sorted[1]!)).toBe(0);
    expect(compareDecisionActions({ kind: "restore_media", mediaId: null }, { kind: "restore_media", mediaId: a })).toBeLessThan(0);
  });
});

describe("textDigest", () => {
  test("the tag names the version of the rule", () => {
    expect(TEXT_DIGEST_TAG).toBe("korbat.text.v1");
  });

  test.each(TEXT_DIGEST_VECTORS.map((vector) => [vector.name, vector] as const))("%s: the sha256 of the tag, a line feed, the salt's bytes and the text's UTF-8 bytes", async (_name, vector) => {
    expect(await textDigest(vector.salt, vector.text)).toBe(vector.digest);
  });

  test("the longest vector is 5000 UTF-16 units, and the vectors hold a line feed, a character outside ASCII and one outside the basic plane", () => {
    expect(Math.max(...TEXT_DIGEST_VECTORS.map((vector) => vector.text.length))).toBe(5000);
    const all = TEXT_DIGEST_VECTORS.map((vector) => vector.text).join("");
    expect(all).toContain(LF);
    expect(all).toContain(E_ACUTE);
    expect(all).toContain(GRINNING);
  });

  test("another salt or another text gives another digest", async () => {
    const digests = await Promise.all([textDigest("a1".repeat(32), "one"), textDigest("a2".repeat(32), "one"), textDigest("a1".repeat(32), "one "), textDigest("a1".repeat(32), "One")]);
    expect(new Set(digests).size).toBe(4);
  });

  test("a salt that is not 32 bytes of lower-case hex is refused, never padded or folded", async () => {
    for (const salt of ["", "a1".repeat(31), "a1".repeat(33), "A1".repeat(32), "g1".repeat(32), ` ${"a1".repeat(32)}`]) {
      await expect(textDigest(salt, "text"), JSON.stringify(salt)).rejects.toThrow(TypeError);
    }
  });

  test("a text with a lone surrogate, which has no UTF-8 bytes, is refused rather than hashed as something else", async () => {
    const high = String.fromCharCode(0xd83d);
    const low = String.fromCharCode(0xde00);
    for (const text of [high, low, `a${high}b`, `${low}${high}`]) await expect(textDigest("a1".repeat(32), text)).rejects.toThrow(TypeError);
    // The pair itself is a character.
    await expect(textDigest("a1".repeat(32), `${high}${low}`)).resolves.toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
  });
});

describe("snapshotText and snapshotDigest", () => {
  const post: SnapshotDigestInput = {
    salt: "ab".repeat(32),
    targetType: "post",
    targetId: "3f1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a",
    takenAt: "2026-10-03T10:00:00.123Z",
    authorHandle: "ada",
    postState: "visible",
    postCreatedAt: "2026-10-01T08:30:00.000Z",
    replyToId: null,
    quoteOfId: "7e2d9a10-6c3b-4f5e-8a21-0d4c7b9e1f36",
    body: `Line one${LF}caf${E_ACUTE} ${GRINNING}`,
    media: [
      { id: "11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555", alt: "A cat", width: 1200, height: 800 },
      { id: "66666666-7777-4888-9999-aaaaaaaaaaaa", alt: null, width: 640, height: 480 },
    ],
    displayName: null,
    bio: null,
    handle: null,
  };
  const account: SnapshotDigestInput = {
    salt: "cd".repeat(32),
    targetType: "account",
    targetId: "8a3c7f0e-1111-4222-8333-944445555666",
    takenAt: "2026-10-03T10:00:00.000Z",
    authorHandle: "bob",
    postState: null,
    postCreatedAt: null,
    replyToId: null,
    quoteOfId: null,
    body: null,
    media: null,
    displayName: `Bob ${GRINNING}`,
    bio: "",
    handle: "bob",
  };
  const BS = String.fromCharCode(92);
  // The texts and the digests below were computed with Python's json and hashlib when they were written.
  const POST_TEXT =
    `{"authorHandle":"ada","bio":null,"body":"Line one${BS}ncaf${E_ACUTE} ${GRINNING}","displayName":null,"handle":null,` +
    `"media":[{"alt":"A cat","height":800,"id":"11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555","width":1200},{"alt":null,"height":480,"id":"66666666-7777-4888-9999-aaaaaaaaaaaa","width":640}],` +
    `"postCreatedAt":"2026-10-01T08:30:00.000Z","postState":"visible","quoteOfId":"7e2d9a10-6c3b-4f5e-8a21-0d4c7b9e1f36","replyToId":null,` +
    `"salt":"${"ab".repeat(32)}","takenAt":"2026-10-03T10:00:00.123Z","targetId":"3f1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a","targetType":"post","v":1}`;
  const POST_DIGEST = "cb995d11ed14e3c4e555c187d319a86506b263e98f924f59f2f7d5231a3bc6e6";
  const ACCOUNT_DIGEST = "41019b2a47d4ebad37cc8c5ad25f8d79a7232c4e3e705231f9e9ba1e02fb1f26";

  test("the tag names the version of the rule", () => {
    expect(SNAPSHOT_DIGEST_TAG).toBe("korbat.snapshot.v1");
  });

  test("the text is the sorted JSON of version 1 and the snapshot's fifteen members", () => {
    expect(snapshotText(post)).toBe(POST_TEXT);
    const parsed = JSON.parse(snapshotText(account)) as Record<string, unknown>;
    expect(Object.keys(parsed)).toEqual(["authorHandle", "bio", "body", "displayName", "handle", "media", "postCreatedAt", "postState", "quoteOfId", "replyToId", "salt", "takenAt", "targetId", "targetType", "v"]);
    expect(parsed).toEqual({ v: 1, ...account });
  });

  test("the digest is the sha256 of the tag, a line feed and that text", async () => {
    expect(await snapshotDigest(post)).toBe(POST_DIGEST);
    expect(await snapshotDigest(account)).toBe(ACCOUNT_DIGEST);
  });

  test("it round-trips the snapshot answer's JSON, whatever order and whatever else the answer carries", async () => {
    // As the console receives it: parsed from JSON, with members the digest does not cover, in another order.
    const sent = {
      id: "9d0f5e3c-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
      digest: POST_DIGEST,
      withheld: false,
      erasedAt: null,
      ...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(post).reverse()),
      media: post.media!.map((image) => ({ height: image.height, width: image.width, note: "never part of a snapshot", alt: image.alt, id: image.id })),
    };
    const answer = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(sent)) as SnapshotDigestInput;
    expect(snapshotText(answer)).toBe(POST_TEXT);
    expect(await snapshotDigest(answer)).toBe(POST_DIGEST);
  });

  test("any member that changes gives another digest", async () => {
    const changed: SnapshotDigestInput[] = [
      { ...post, salt: "ac".repeat(32) },
      { ...post, takenAt: "2026-10-03T10:00:00.124Z" },
      { ...post, body: `${post.body} ` },
      { ...post, postState: "withheld" },
      { ...post, quoteOfId: null },
      { ...post, media: [post.media![1]!, post.media![0]!] },
      { ...post, media: [{ ...post.media![0]!, alt: "A dog" }, post.media![1]!] },
      { ...post, authorHandle: "adb" },
    ];
    const digests = await Promise.all([post, ...changed].map(snapshotDigest));
    expect(new Set(digests).size).toBe(changed.length + 1);
  });

  test("a time that is not the UTC string toISOString writes, to the millisecond, is refused", () => {
    for (const takenAt of ["2026-10-03T10:00:00Z", "2026-10-03T10:00:00.123456Z", "2026-10-03T12:00:00.123+02:00", "2026-10-03 10:00:00.123Z", ""]) {
      expect(() => snapshotText({ ...post, takenAt }), takenAt).toThrow(TypeError);
    }
    expect(() => snapshotText({ ...post, postCreatedAt: "2026-10-01T08:30:00Z" })).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(snapshotText({ ...post, takenAt: new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 9, 3, 10, 0, 0, 123)).toISOString() })).toBe(POST_TEXT);
  });
});

describe("appealDeadline", () => {
  const at = (iso: string) => new Date(iso);
  const deadline = (iso: string) => appealDeadline(at(iso)).toISOString();

  test("six calendar months later, at the same UTC time", () => {
    expect(deadline("2026-10-03T10:15:30.250Z")).toBe("2027-04-03T10:15:30.250Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-01-15T00:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2026-07-15T00:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-07-01T23:59:59.999Z")).toBe("2027-01-01T23:59:59.999Z");
  });

  test("a day the sixth month lacks becomes that month's last day", () => {
    // 31 August plus six months is the end of February: the 28th, or the 29th in a leap year.
    expect(deadline("2026-08-31T12:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2027-02-28T12:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2027-08-31T12:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2027-08-30T12:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2027-08-29T12:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-03-31T08:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2026-09-30T08:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-05-31T08:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2026-11-30T08:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-10-31T08:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2027-04-30T08:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-12-31T08:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2027-06-30T08:00:00.000Z");
    // A leap day itself moves to 29 August: August has the day.
    expect(deadline("2028-02-29T08:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2028-08-29T08:00:00.000Z");
  });

  test("it is computed in UTC: the last instants of a UTC month stay on that month's side", () => {
    expect(deadline("2026-08-31T23:59:59.999Z")).toBe("2027-02-28T23:59:59.999Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2027-03-01T00:00:00.000Z");
  });

  test("it leaves its argument as it was", () => {
    const informed = at("2026-08-31T12:00:00.000Z");
    appealDeadline(informed);
    expect(informed.toISOString()).toBe("2026-08-31T12:00:00.000Z");
  });
});

### Create `apps/api/src/cli/counts.ts`

```ts
/**
 * The yearly counts (3f design, section 2 row 40, sections 7.18 and 8.11, "Recovery and the counts"):
 *
 *   docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm migrate node dist/staff.js tco-counts <year>
 *
 * Each January the operator prints, for the calendar year before in UTC, the figures that TCO Art. 7(3) and 21(1) ask
 * of a host, and publishes them by hand before 1 March when any is not zero (the README's "The yearly counts"; 3d prints
 * them on the transparency page later). It runs as the migrator, as every command of 3f does, since only the migrator
 * reads the productions; in one read-only transaction at one snapshot, and it writes no audit row: it changes nothing.
 *
 * Every figure is counted from rows, and a figure the rows can no longer give prints "not recorded", never 0, so that a
 * published zero is always a true one. The rows a year's figures rest on are the orders of that year (by their receipt,
 * or by their opening when nobody recorded a receipt), their items by the time each was disabled and their events by
 * the time each took effect; the ledger's decisions by when they were decided; the productions by when each was opened;
 * and the audit log's rows by when each was written. An order's records go three years after its last event, and a
 * production's with it (6.8), while the ledger and the audit log stay: so the order figures are "not recorded" for a year
 * in which the retention job erased the records of a removal order that could have held a row of it, and the authority's
 * accesses for a year whose audit rows name a production that is gone. A message at the contact point is deleted 30 days
 * after it was handled, so the referrals are counted from the audit rows `contact_closed`, which keep the disposition.
 *
 * This file has no entry point of its own, so both bundles can include it (build.mjs says why that matters).
 */
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { ANNEX3_GROUNDS, ORDER_GROUNDS, type Annex3Ground, type OrderGround } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Db, DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { Refusal, refuse, rows, type OrderDone } from "./orders";

/** The counting commands, each with its first lines of STAFF_USAGE. */
export const COUNT_COMMANDS = ["tco-counts"] as const;
export type CountCommandName = (typeof COUNT_COMMANDS)[number];

export const COUNT_USAGE = [
  `${"  tco-counts <year>".padEnd(41)}print the figures of TCO Art. 7(3) and 21(1) for that calendar year in UTC, from rows,`,
  `${"".padEnd(41)}and "not recorded" for a figure the rows cannot give; read-only; run it in the migrate service`,
];

export type CountCommand = { command: "tco-counts"; year: number };

/** A calendar year as the operator types it: four digits, never with a leading zero. */
const YEAR = /^[1-9][0-9]{3}$/;

/** Reads a counting command's words. */
export function parseCountArgs(command: CountCommandName, rest: readonly string[]): CountCommand {
  if (rest.length !== 1 || !YEAR.test(rest[0]!)) throw new Error(`${command}: takes one calendar year of four digits, as 2026`);
  return { command, year: Number(rest[0]) };
}

/** The figures of one year; null is a figure the rows can no longer give. */
export interface TcoCounts {
  year: number;
  /** Removal orders received, by issuing state in code order, and how many came from another Member State. */
  received: { total: number; byState: [string, number][]; crossBorder: number } | null;
  /** The items of removal orders disabled in the year. */
  itemsDisabled: number | null;
  /**
   * For each removal order of the year whose every item is disabled or closed and of which at least one was disabled: the
   * minutes from its clock's start to the disabling of its last item, in ascending order, null for an order whose receipt
   * nobody recorded (after the numbers); how many of them were outside the hour (an effect given while the clock was
   * stopped counts as inside, as legal_order_clock judges it); how many of them that judgement cannot be made for; and how
   * many of the year's orders still have an item open.
   */
  minutes: { list: (number | null)[]; outside: number; withoutReceipt: number; open: number } | null;
  /** Annex III sent, by ground. */
  annex3: Record<Annex3Ground, number> | null;
  /** Scrutiny asked for, and its outcomes. */
  scrutiny: { requested: number; annulled: number; upheld: number } | null;
  /** Items reinstated, by ground. */
  reinstated: Record<OrderGround, number> | null;
  /** Accesses to preserved content by an authority: productions of the instrument preserved_access for an authority. */
  authorityAccess: number | null;
  /** Final decisions of korbat's own that restricted something as terrorist content, without an order. */
  terroristWithoutOrder: number;
  /** Messages at the contact point closed as a referral. */
  referralsClosed: number;
}

/** Reads the figures of a calendar year in UTC, on the caller's transaction, which reads as the migrator. */
export async function tcoCounts(tx: DbTx, year: number): Promise<TcoCounts> {
  const from = sql`make_timestamptz(${year}::int, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 'UTC')`;
  const to = sql`make_timestamptz(${year + 1}::int, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 'UTC')`;

  // Whether the retention job erased the records of a removal order that could have held a row of this year: the order
  // was received (or opened) before the year ended, and its last row was at most record_keep_years before its erasure.
  // The audit log keeps both rows that say so, the opening with the order's kind and receipt and the erasure's step.
  const [ordersErased] = await rows<{ erased: boolean }>(
    tx,
    sql`select exists (
          select 1 from public.audit_log r
            join public.audit_log o on o.action = 'order_opened' and o.target_id = r.metadata->>'orderId'
           cross join public.order_rules() k
           where r.action = 'moderation_retention' and r.metadata->>'step' = 'order_records'
             and o.metadata->>'kind' = 'tco_removal'
             and coalesce((o.metadata->>'receivedAt')::timestamptz, o.created_at) < ${to}
             and r.created_at - make_interval(years => k.record_keep_years) >= ${from}) as erased`,
  );

  const orders = await rows<{ member_state: string; cross_border: boolean; items_open: number; finished: boolean; within_hour: boolean | null; minutes: number | null }>(
    tx,
    sql`select o.member_state, o.cross_border, c.items_open,
               (c.items_open = 0 and c.last_effect_at is not null) as finished, c.within_hour,
               floor(extract(epoch from (c.last_effect_at - c.clock_start)) / 60)::int as minutes
          from public.legal_orders o
          join public.legal_order_clock c on c.order_id = o.id
         where o.kind = 'tco_removal' and coalesce(o.received_at, o.opened_at) >= ${from} and coalesce(o.received_at, o.opened_at) < ${to}`,
  );
  const [disabled] = await rows<{ n: number }>(
    tx,
    sql`select count(*)::int as n from public.legal_order_items t join public.legal_orders o on o.id = t.order_id
         where o.kind = 'tco_removal' and t.disabled_at >= ${from} and t.disabled_at < ${to}`,
  );
  const events = await rows<{ kind: string; ground: string | null; n: number }>(
    tx,
    sql`select e.kind, e.ground, count(*)::int as n from public.legal_order_events e join public.legal_orders o on o.id = e.order_id
         where o.kind = 'tco_removal' and e.kind in ('annex3_sent', 'scrutiny_requested', 'scrutiny_decided', 'reinstated')
           and coalesce(e.effective_at, e.at) >= ${from} and coalesce(e.effective_at, e.at) < ${to}
         group by e.kind, e.ground`,
  );

  // An authority's access is recorded twice: as its production, which the retention job erases with the order's records,
  // and in the audit row preserved_accessed, which names the production and stays.
  const [access] = await rows<{ n: number; erased: boolean }>(
    tx,
    sql`select (select count(*)::int from public.productions p
                 where p.instrument = 'preserved_access' and p.purpose = 'authority' and p.opened_at >= ${from} and p.opened_at < ${to}) as n,
               exists (select 1 from public.audit_log a
                        where a.action = 'preserved_accessed' and a.metadata->>'purpose' = 'authority' and a.created_at >= ${from} and a.created_at < ${to}
                          and not exists (select 1 from public.productions p where p.id::text = a.metadata->>'productionId')) as erased`,
  );
  // korbat's own final decisions on terrorist content, which the ledger keeps for good; an order's decision is of the kind order.
  const [terrorist] = await rows<{ n: number }>(
    tx,
    sql`select count(*)::int as n from public.decisions d
         where d.kind::text = 'final' and d.outcome::text = 'restricted' and d.category_keyword = 'KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT'
           and d.decided_at >= ${from} and d.decided_at < ${to}`,
  );
  const [referrals] = await rows<{ n: number }>(
    tx,
    sql`select count(*)::int as n from public.audit_log a
         where a.action = 'contact_closed' and a.metadata->>'disposition' = 'referral' and a.created_at >= ${from} and a.created_at < ${to}`,
  );

  const eventCount = (kind: string, ground: string | null = null) =>
    events.filter((row) => row.kind === kind && (ground === null || row.ground === ground)).reduce((sum, row) => sum + row.n, 0);
  const byState = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const order of orders) byState.set(order.member_state, (byState.get(order.member_state) ?? 0) + 1);
  const finished = orders.filter((order) => order.finished);
  const known = finished.filter((order) => order.minutes !== null).map((order) => order.minutes!).sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const erased = ordersErased!.erased;

  return {
    year,
    received: erased
      ? null
      : { total: orders.length, byState: [...byState.entries()].sort(([a], [b]) => (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0)), crossBorder: orders.filter((order) => order.cross_border).length },
    itemsDisabled: erased ? null : disabled!.n,
    minutes: erased
      ? null
      : {
          list: [...known, ...finished.filter((order) => order.minutes === null).map(() => null)],
          outside: finished.filter((order) => order.within_hour === false).length,
          withoutReceipt: finished.filter((order) => order.within_hour === null).length,
          open: orders.filter((order) => order.items_open > 0).length,
        },
    annex3: erased ? null : (Object.fromEntries(ANNEX3_GROUNDS.map((ground) => [ground, eventCount("annex3_sent", ground)])) as Record<Annex3Ground, number>),
    scrutiny: erased ? null : { requested: eventCount("scrutiny_requested"), annulled: eventCount("scrutiny_decided", "annulled"), upheld: eventCount("scrutiny_decided", "upheld") },
    reinstated: erased ? null : (Object.fromEntries(ORDER_GROUNDS.map((ground) => [ground, eventCount("reinstated", ground)])) as Record<OrderGround, number>),
    authorityAccess: access!.erased ? null : access!.n,
    terroristWithoutOrder: terrorist!.n,
    referralsClosed: referrals!.n,
  };
}

const NOT_RECORDED = "not recorded";

/** The figures as the command prints them: a line a figure, each starting with the command's name (8.11). */
export function describeTcoCounts(counts: TcoCounts): string[] {
  const line = (text: string) => `tco-counts: ${text}`;
  const { received, minutes } = counts;
  const states = received === null ? [] : received.byState.map(([state, n]) => `${state}: ${n}`);
  const receivedText = received === null ? NOT_RECORDED : `${received.total} (${states.length > 0 ? `${states.join(", ")}; ` : ""}from another Member State: ${received.crossBorder})`;
  const minutesText = (() => {
    if (minutes === null) return NOT_RECORDED;
    const list = minutes.list.length === 0 ? "none" : minutes.list.map((m) => (m === null ? NOT_RECORDED : String(m))).join(", ");
    const outside =
      minutes.withoutReceipt > 0 ? `${NOT_RECORDED} (${minutes.withoutReceipt} ${minutes.withoutReceipt === 1 ? "order" : "orders"} without a recorded receipt)` : String(minutes.outside);
    return `${list}; outside the hour: ${outside}; with an item still open: ${minutes.open}`;
  })();
  const byGround = <G extends string>(grounds: readonly G[], figures: Record<G, number> | null) =>
    figures === null ? NOT_RECORDED : grounds.map((ground) => `${ground} ${figures[ground]}`).join(", ");
  const figure = (n: number | null) => (n === null ? NOT_RECORDED : String(n));
  return [
    line(`removal orders received: ${receivedText}`),
    line(`items disabled following a removal order: ${figure(counts.itemsDisabled)}`),
    line(`minutes from the clock's start to the disabling of an order's last item: ${minutesText}`),
    line(`Annex III sent, by ground: ${byGround(ANNEX3_GROUNDS, counts.annex3)}`),
    line(`scrutiny: ${counts.scrutiny === null ? NOT_RECORDED : `requested ${counts.scrutiny.requested}; annulled ${counts.scrutiny.annulled}; upheld ${counts.scrutiny.upheld}`}`),
    line(`reinstated, by ground: ${byGround(ORDER_GROUNDS, counts.reinstated)}`),
    line(`access to preserved content by an authority: ${figure(counts.authorityAccess)}`),
    line(`restricted by korbat as terrorist content without an order: ${counts.terroristWithoutOrder}`),
    line(`referrals closed: ${counts.referralsClosed}`),
  ];
}

/**
 * tco-counts on the migrator's own connection: one transaction at one snapshot, read-only, with the command line's
 * 10-second lock timeout. A year that has not begun has nothing to count and is refused.
 */
export async function countCommand(migrateDb: Db, cmd: CountCommand, now: Date = new Date()): Promise<OrderDone> {
  try {
    if (cmd.year > now.getUTCFullYear()) refuse(cmd.command, `the year ${cmd.year} has not begun`);
    const counts = await migrateDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
      await tx.execute(sql`set transaction isolation level repeatable read, read only`);
      await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
      return tcoCounts(tx, cmd.year);
    });
    return { ok: true, lines: describeTcoCounts(counts) };
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof Refusal) return { ok: false, problem: err.message };
    throw err;
  }
}
```

# korbat

Pseudonymous social platform with a narrow public rulebook and transparent moderation. Self-hosted.

- Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-korbat-design.md`
- Accounts and sessions (sub-project 1a): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-identity-auth-1a-design.md`
- Posting and feed (sub-project 2a): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-17-posting-feed-2a-design.md`
- Plans: `docs/superpowers/plans/`

## Dev quick start
```bash
pnpm install
node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs                # creates or completes infra/.env, apps/api/.env, apps/app/.env and apps/worker/.env, and derives apps/api/.env.test; values are random and never printed
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml up -d postgres redis mailpit   # dev host ports 55432, 56379, 51025, 58025 (movable: DEV_*_PORT in infra/.env)
pnpm --filter @korbat/api dev               # http://localhost:3000/api/health; reads apps/api/.env
pnpm --filter @korbat/worker dev            # the image worker; reads apps/worker/.env and works on .data/media
pnpm --filter @korbat/app web               # http://localhost:8081
pnpm --filter @korbat/admin dev             # the staff console at http://localhost:8090 (never 127.0.0.1); forwards /api/staff/* to the API above
```

Emails sent in development (sign-in codes, new-device alerts, lockout notices) land in Mailpit at http://localhost:58025. Locally the web app uses Cloudflare's always-pass Turnstile test key, so the human check never blocks you.

The data services are PostgreSQL 18 and Valkey (the BSD-licensed fork of Redis, still under the service name `redis`, on its own volume `valkeydata`: Valkey 9 cannot read the RDB format 12 that Redis 7.4 wrote into the old `redisdata` volume, which held only transient state and can be removed with `docker volume rm`). Valkey needs the password from `infra/.env`; `gen-dev-env` writes it into the API's `REDIS_URL` too, so an older `.env` is fixed by running it again.

korbat once ran MinIO and never used it. Images live on two Docker volumes instead, `media-uploads` and `media-store`. If an old stack left a `korbat_miniodata` volume behind, `docker volume rm korbat_miniodata` removes it.

## Tests
```bash
pnpm test                                     # unit tests of every package
node scripts/test-db.mjs                      # creates or migrates the korbat_test database; run it again after adding a migration
pnpm --filter @korbat/api test:integration    # needs postgres, redis and mailpit up
```

Integration tests have their own database, `korbat_test`, and their own Redis database, 15. Both are named in `apps/api/.env.test`, which `node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` derives from `apps/api/.env`. Every run starts by emptying them, and refuses to start if a URL points anywhere else, so tests never touch development data.

Before they had their own database, the integration suites left accounts, profiles and posts in the development database, and the smoke test still leaves its first account per run, by then a moderator, with one open moderation case on that account's post. To see and remove them:

```bash
node scripts/clean-dev-fixtures.mjs          # lists test accounts and profiles without an account; deletes nothing
node scripts/clean-dev-fixtures.mjs --yes    # deletes them with everything they made
```

It only matches emails of the tests' shape, `<word>-<uuid>@korbat.local`, recomputes the counters of kept profiles and posts they touched, and refuses to run unless `API_APP_ORIGIN` in `infra/.env` is a localhost origin. It keeps an account that holds a staff key or that the moderation record names (one that decided anything, one on either side of a staff link, the subject of a case that a decision or a reveal names), and counts it as kept; every other case about a deleted account or one of its posts is deleted with it, the smoke test's open case included.

## Full stack
```bash
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml up -d --build   # http://localhost:8080, and the staff console at http://localhost:8090
node scripts/smoke-auth-stack.mjs --base http://localhost:8080 --console http://localhost:8090 --mailpit http://localhost:58025 --terms draft-2026-09 -- docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml
```

The smoke test first checks the staff console's site: its page carries the console's own policy and is never stored, and the staff API answers there (401 without a session) and nowhere else (Caddy's own 404 on the app's site); the console's case routes (the overview, the queue, a case, the appeals) answer the same two ways, and the console's site refuses the app's own moderation routes with a 404 of its own. It then signs up a throwaway account through Caddy, reads its code from Mailpit, posts and reads the post back from the public Latest timeline. It uploads a JPEG carrying a GPS position, posts it, and checks that the served file is a fresh WebP without metadata, that a symlink planted in the store from inside the worker gets a 404, and that deleting the post removes the image from disk. It checks the worker's isolation, then grants the account a staff role with the CLI and checks that its session was revoked. A second throwaway account edits its bio, changes its handle, reports the first account's post under a rule, finds that report undecided in its own list and as the last member, `moderation`, of its export, and deletes itself. Last, signed out, a notice that the same post is illegal is taken with the human check: it answers a reference and a token, the status page opens with that token, the receipt arrives in Mailpit, and the token in the receipt's link opens the same page. Nothing in it decides the case, since a decision needs a staff key: every run leaves one open case in lane 2 on the first account's post. One network can run it five times an hour and twenty times a day, since its two sign-ups count against the hourly sign-up limit and its signed-out notice against the limits of reports sent without an account.

After every sharp upgrade, add `--worst-case`: it also uploads flat-colour files at the pixel caps (48 MP 16-bit interlaced PNG, 48 MP progressive JPEG, 48 MP GIF, 16 MP AVIF), expects each to be ready without the worker being OOM-killed or restarted, and prints the worker's memory peak.

Caddy listens on 8080 inside its container as its own user, proxies `/api` to the API and serves the web app with the page's security headers; `index.html` is revalidated on every load and the hashed bundles are cached for a year. On 8090 it serves the staff console under the console's own policy and proxies only `/api/staff/*`, which the app's site refuses. On 8091 it serves the phones' push site: only the two alert topics' subscriptions reach ntfy, and every other path is Caddy's own 404. The compose file keeps cloudflared, Caddy, the API and the data services on separate networks, so cloudflared reaches only Caddy and Caddy only the API and ntfy. Under the Compose profile `notify`, the contact point's watcher (`notify`) and the push server (ntfy) join two networks of their own: `push`, which has no route out and whose clients the app's and the console's sites refuse with 403, and `watch`, which holds the watcher and PostgreSQL and nothing else. With the profile on, add `--push http://localhost:8091` to the smoke test: it checks that the push site answers ntfy's own API with 404 and hands a subscription to ntfy, and that from the push network the app's and the console's sites answer 403.

## Upgrading PostgreSQL

The stack runs PostgreSQL 18 on the `pgdata18` volume. A database from the earlier PostgreSQL 16 volume (`pgdata`) is moved by:

```bash
node scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs -- docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml
```

It dumps the old cluster with the old image in a throwaway container, starts the new server, restores the dump with every owner kept, and compares the row counts. The old volume stays until you remove it; the test database is created again by `node scripts/test-db.mjs`. Run `staff.js audit-verify` with every kept place before and after a major upgrade; Before going public says why.

## Upgrading

Authorities' orders and the alert channel (sub-project 3f) add a database role for the contact point's watcher, two services under a Compose profile, the hand-over's service under another, the report hold, and two arguments of the web build.

- On a database that exists, give the role its password and create it, with its USAGE on the schema `public`, once, as the superuser and against korbat's own database, before the first 3f migration: set `KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD` in `infra/.env` (`node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` does in development), run `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d postgres`, which passes it to the database's container, then the command below. Run twice, it changes nothing. The grant cannot be made by the migration: the migrator does not own the schema, and its grant would be a warning and nothing more. The migration checks both and stops with "create the role korbat_notify first" when either is missing, so a half-done upgrade stops there and not at a watcher that cannot read a row. A new data directory gets both from `infra/postgres/init/01-roles.sh`.

```bash
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml exec -T postgres sh -c 'psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" -v pw="$KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD"' <<'SQL'
SET korbat.notify_pw = :'pw';
DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'korbat_notify') THEN
  IF current_setting('korbat.notify_pw') = '' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD is empty in the postgres container: set it in infra/.env, then up -d postgres'; END IF;
  EXECUTE format('CREATE ROLE korbat_notify LOGIN PASSWORD %L', current_setting('korbat.notify_pw'));
END IF; END $$;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO korbat_notify;
SQL
```

- `notify` and ntfy run under the Compose profile `notify`. Switch it on in one place, `COMPOSE_PROFILES=notify` in `infra/.env`, which Compose reads for every command: the README's commands stay as they are, and an upgrade then recreates the two services with the rest. Without that line they are never started, or keep running an old image against a migrated database.
- Until the contact-point mailbox exists, leave the profile off and set `API_NOTIFY=off`: korbat then says on the console's home screen that phone alerts are switched off on this server, and mails no "Phone alerts are down". No setting of `notify`, ntfy or the hand-over is needed for the stack to start.
- The hand-over's service (`handover`) runs under the Compose profile `handover`, which stays off: the operator starts it by hand for one hand-over, with the directory on its command line (Authorities' orders, Notifications and hand-overs). It needs no setting.
- The report hold is on from the upgrade: while a report of sealed images to the authorities is owed, the deletion of the account keeps its address, and nothing else, for at most 7 days. `API_REPORT_HOLD=off` in `infra/.env` ends the practice for everyone and deletes as before; set it only on counsel's advice.
- The web build takes `WEB_CONTACT_POINT` and `WEB_HOME_STATE` from `infra/.env` for the terms (the contact point for authorities and korbat's Member State). Neither is required, and both stay empty, or the state alone set, until the last step of Before going public; `node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` adds the two lines to an existing file without changing a value. Rebuild the caddy image after a change of either.

## Restoring

Restore the database and the `media-store` volume from the same moment. The API's sweeper deletes images that have no row: after a database restored from an older snapshot it would delete every image posted since. It refuses when there are many such images, but for a restore window set `MEDIA_RECONCILE=off` in `infra/.env` before starting the API, and put it back to `on` once the store matches the database. `force` makes one pass delete them anyway, for when they really are orphans.

Keep no backup of the database or of `media-store` more than 30 days after it was taken (`RETENTION.backupDays`, which the terms publish), and delete older ones, except a backup that korbat must keep for the authorities (step 5), which you keep until they have answered. A backup holds what korbat erased after it was taken, among it content erased under rule R4.

The staff steps run with the api service stopped (`docker compose -f infra/compose.yml stop api`), before it starts again, with the commands under Staff console and Moderation; step 5 says which of its parts wait until the API runs again:

1. Run `staff.js audit-head` on the restored database. Its place and hash go to the keeper with the restore's date: new rows will take the places lost with the backup's later rows, with other hashes, so every place kept after the backup would fail as a rewrite does. The keeper retires those places with that note, `audit-verify` runs from then on with the places at or before the restored one, and a failing place that no announced restore explains is a rewrite.
2. Run `staff.js revoke <email> all` for every account `staff.js keys` lists, since the restore brings back every staff key, staff session and enrolment link revoked or cancelled after the backup, and the auth events and audit rows that recorded those revocations are gone with it.
3. Run grant-role for every staff account with the role on your own list, and `user` for any other account `staff.js keys` lists, as after an API incident: it sets back any role changed after the backup and ends every session and staff session of the account, app sessions revoked after the backup included. Then compare the accounts `staff.js keys` lists with that list.
4. Each person enrols again, two keys each.
5. Moderation. Every decision, review and seal confirmed after the backup is gone with its audit rows, and what it restricted is back: sealed images are served again, and a removed post is public again. Reports, notices and re-examinations received after the backup are gone too, and so is everything `staff.js` wrote since: links and unlinks and limits. So are the stops that people pressed on a report's page after the backup, and the report mail that accounts resumed in Settings since; korbat may mail such an address about reports again, though its holder asked it to stop, until they press stop again, and an account that resumed its report mail gets none until it resumes again. Nothing on the server or in your records names them, so none can be applied again. Nothing on the restored server names the lost decisions either: the keeper's daily copy names them, and the orders and records to authorities, up to the keeper's last download, and Restoring with the keeper's copy below takes each lost measure again from it. So before the api service starts again after step 3, set `APP_SITE=closed` in `infra/.env`, which closes the app's site and leaves the console's open, as that block's first step says. Before it starts, also delete the moderation dispatch's daily markers, which live in Valkey and are not restored with the database: `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml exec -T redis sh -c 'export VALKEYCLI_AUTH="$REDIS_PASSWORD"; valkey-cli --scan --pattern "*moderation-dispatched:*" | while read -r k; do valkey-cli del "$k"; done'`. The dispatch's first round then releases again every outcome and changed outcome that was answered before the day's dispatch hour and not yet released at the backup, so the status pages, the re-examination windows and the mails agree again; a person whose outcome mail or statement went out after the backup's time gets it a second time. Before it starts, also set `API_MODERATION_RETENTION=off` in `infra/.env`. The restored database no longer holds the cases, freezes and seals made after the backup. From its first round, 10 minutes after the start, the retention job would make R4 redactions final, erase case evidence and delete the images that these cases, freezes and seals no longer protect. That includes images sealed and reported to the police since the backup, long before an admin has enrolled and sealed them again. While the switch is off nothing is erased or deleted, and the console's count of late erasures rises. Before anyone decides anything, run `staff.js link` and `staff.js unlink` until the links match your records, and check that the count `staff.js keys` prints for each staff account equals your records'; then run `staff.js limits` with the numbers you last set. Once the staff have enrolled again, an admin first opens a finding citing R2 on every post or account that your R2 records show was sealed after the backup's time, unless its case is open in the restored database, and seals its images again. Only then, once every such seal has been applied again, set `API_MODERATION_RETENTION=on` in `infra/.env` and run `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d api`, which recreates the API with it, and open the app's site again when the console's After a restore screen says so (`APP_SITE=open`). Its next rounds make up the erasures that fell due meanwhile. Then tell the authority each of these was reported to what was lost and when it was sealed again, and keep the backup you restored from until that authority has answered, also past the 30 days. Sub-project 3d adds the release of sealed images and its replay after a restore. Then the cases that were open at the backup are open again in the queue: decide them again at once, lane 0 first. Each moderator also opens a finding on any other target they remember restricting since the backup's time.

**Restoring with the keeper's copy** (sub-project 3f). The keeper's daily copy of the audit log's tail (Staff console, the audit log's "Download since my last copy") names the orders, the records to authorities and the decisions the backup lacks, up to the keeper's last download. These steps come after the staff steps above; where they and step 5 differ, these hold.

1. Before the API starts: `API_MODERATION_RETENTION=off`, `MEDIA_RECONCILE=off` and `APP_SITE=closed` in `infra/.env` (the app's site then answers 503 to every path; the console's site is unchanged).
2. Feed the import every keeper's file from the one that holds the restored head's place onward, oldest first, concatenated on standard input: `cat <files> | docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js restore-import <kept places>` (`-T`: without it Compose attaches a terminal and the redirect fails). The files need not start at the head: the import checks the earlier lines and skips them. A changed file is refused whole and nothing is written; a hole between two files is printed, and what lies behind it is not imported. Read what it prints, a hole among it.
3. Compare the contact-point mailbox since the keeper's last download with the orders it lists; open what is missing with `order-open --received`. An imported item whose link named no post shows `sha256:` and a digest in place of the link, since the copy holds no link's text: read the address from the order in the mailbox. Enter the records of class "record" again from the authority's letters, each with its command and `--gap <gap>`, which closes that gap. Until the last of them is entered, answer no data request: `access-request` cannot print an authority's "not to the person" mark for a record that is still lost.
4. Before any order's disabling is taken again: compare each held notice the import lists with the mailbox since the keeper's last download. An extension or a later time that was recorded after that download is lost with the restore; record it again first (`order-hold-extend`, `order-hold-until`), or the disabling taken again would tell the author at the old end.
5. Start the API; everyone enrols new keys.
6. On the console's After a restore screen, take every measure again, from the top. An order's disabling first: its hour, its preservation and its hold are the old ones. A gap that needs nothing is closed by an admin as "Not needed", with the key.
7. When the screen says so, set `APP_SITE=open`; when it says so, switch retention and the sweep back on (`API_MODERATION_RETENTION=on`, `MEDIA_RECONCILE=on`).

The keeper's file holds no post and no statement, but it names authorities and references, held orders' among them, and a reference may itself name a person: keep it like the head, not like a log.

A suspect or revoked staff key is never cleared or revived.

## Posting and feed
Text posts up to 1000 characters, replies, quotes, likes, reposts and bookmarks; follows, blocks and mutes; a chronological Following timeline and a public Latest timeline; threads and profile pages. The web app's home is the timeline; sign-in lives at `/signin`.

- **Reading signed out:** Latest, threads and profiles are public. Following, bookmarks, likes, follower lists and privacy settings need a session.
- **Blocks** are enforced in every query, not just the interface: neither account sees the other while signed in, follows are removed both ways, and the blocked side gets `not_found` so nothing is revealed. Posts are public, so a block does not hide them from someone who signs out; the interface says so.
- **Mutes** are one-way and silent, and hide an account from your timelines only.
- **Liker lists are never exposed.** Counts are public; likes and bookmarks are private to their owner.
- **Write limits** per account, tiered by account age: in the first 24 hours 5 posts and 20 replies an hour and no reposts or quotes for 48 hours; afterwards 30 posts and 60 replies an hour. Everyone: 100 likes an hour, 50 follows an hour and 400 a day, 30 blocks or mutes an hour. Undo actions are never limited.
- **Deleting** blanks the text in the database and leaves a tombstone only where a thread or a quote needs it. There is no editing. A post that a report or a moderator's finding named before it was deleted keeps a copy with its case, read by staff only, for as long as the case needs it (Moderation, Evidence and retention).
- **Moderation states.** A post is `visible`, `withheld` (while a case about it is being decided) or `removed`, as the database derives it from the measures that moderators' decisions recorded; nothing else writes the state, and the API's role cannot.
