- New section "How moderators decide", which states: that a moderator, never a program, decides every case; which decisions only an admin takes (6.2 step 6: every final decision, acting or not, on a report or finding under R2 or R5 or made on the anonymous path, every lifting of a seal, and their corrections), and that any moderator may hide a reported threat from others, or seal reported images, at once until then; that on the path for child sexual abuse material a moderator and an admin decide without seeing the images, on the report and on what korbat can read, and that nobody at korbat opens images that are reported or found as such material while the report is unanswered or the images are sealed, which covers the images of a post while such a report about it or about its author's profile is unanswered; that after an admin has answered without a seal, staff may open them like any other image; that reports on other grounds about those images, corrections and appeals are meanwhile decided on what korbat can read or wait, that an admin's answer to such a report about a post also answers the earlier reports about that post, and that whoever sent a report about a post that is answered without action while its images cannot be opened is told so and may ask again; that the seal can cover every image on a profile's posts, hides them from their author too from the first seal, and never hides a post's text; that a report about a post that quotes another opens a case on the quoted post too; that a moderator never decides about their own accounts or accounts close to them; the measures (`MEASURES`: while deciding, a post or one of its images hidden from others, a display name or bio reset; when the case is decided, a post removed, one image removed, a display name or bio reset; and, while deciding or when the case is decided, the images a case covers sealed); that a reset is written once and korbat does not put the old value back: the person may set the field again, and what they set is judged on its own if someone reports it; that korbat restricts the least it can (one image rather than the post, one field rather than the account); that every finding of a breach is recorded as a restriction of its own, also when the content was already not shown or deleted, and its statement then says that it changed nothing now; that every decision that restricts your content, also one that changes nothing anyone sees now, every decision that reverses one, every answer to your appeal, and every end or lift of something korbat told you it did while deciding comes with a statement of reasons, in the app at once and by email; that a decision to take no action is not sent to you, since it would tell you that someone reported you, unless it ends or lifts something korbat told you it did while deciding; that something korbat does while deciding about a post you had already deleted is recorded without being sent to you, since it can never take effect; and that content restricted for being illegal is restricted everywhere, since korbat cannot restrict by country.
- New section "Appeals", which states (6.3, 7.7): that the person a final decision restricts may appeal it once, while any of it is in force, within six months of being told, free and with no form to follow, with "Appeal" on the decision's screen under Settings, Cases, at most five a day; that what korbat does while it decides cannot be appealed, ends with the case's final decision (shown, sent, and appealable when it restricts; a seal ends with an admin's answer to the reports it was taken on), and may be lifted earlier by a moderator (a seal only by an admin); who reviews (a moderator who made none of the case's decisions, including hiding the content while it was decided, did not report it, and has no link to anyone in the case), and that the appeal waits, without a time limit and saying so on its screen, while korbat has no such moderator: with one moderator every appeal, with two every case both took part in (one hid the content or reported it and the other decided it, which is how direct threats and images reported as child sexual abuse material are handled whenever the moderator on duty is not the admin); that a review keeps the decision, lifts part of it or lifts all of it, and never adds to it; that korbat does not put back a display name or bio it reset (set it again; the screen of the decision that reset it shows what it was while korbat keeps the case's copies, and for at least 30 days after a reset that is lifted or ends before they are erased, unless korbat had already erased a value reset under R4, as Your data says); that a decision reversed in full can no longer be appealed, since nothing of it remains; the seal's rules (an appeal of a seal waits, without a time limit, for the assessment of the authority korbat reported the images to; only an admin lifts a seal, and a seal for good only on that authority's answer that they are not child sexual abuse material); that a decision changed on review or by a correction is final within korbat, and everyone whose report it answered is told; and that you can also go to court, or complain to the Digital Services Coordinator of the EU country where you live.
- New section "Terrorist content" (TCO Art. 7(1)): korbat removes terrorist content as defined in Article 2(7) of Regulation (EU) 2021/784 when it is told about it in a notice, and, once korbat is open to the public, complies with an authority's removal order within one hour; material for educational, journalistic, artistic or research purposes, or for preventing or countering terrorism, and polemic or controversial views in public debate are not terrorist content (Art. 1(3)); korbat uses no automated tool to find it.
- "Your data" gains, with the periods of `RETENTION` (6.6): what korbat keeps when someone reports a post or a profile, whatever the decision (a copy of its text, and its images held; for a report of child sexual abuse material, the images of the reported post, of the post it quotes or of all a profile's posts, kept, shown to nobody once their post is deleted, also when their author deletes the post or the account, until an admin has answered it; images an admin then keeps sealed, with korbat's copies of their post's text, are kept for the authorities, are left out of the account's export, and are not released by korbat on its own), and that deleting a post or the account leaves these copies until their period ends; that a case's copies go about a day after the case closes unless a restriction of it can still be appealed or, for a post, a report that only an admin can answer still waits or its images are sealed; that content korbat removes or resets under rule R4 (doxxing), a post's text, an image, a display name or a bio, is erased for good, as far as that decision still stands, once it can no longer be appealed (six months after you were told) or your appeal against it is answered (for a post, later only while a report that only an admin can answer still waits or while its images are sealed): from your own view, your export and the decision's screen, and every copy korbat keeps of it but its backups (an image once no other case still holds it), also when you had deleted the post, so a later reversal cannot bring it back or show it to you again; that korbat's backups of its database and images hold everything as it stood when each was taken, what korbat erased since included, and are deleted {backupDays} days after they were taken, except a backup that korbat must keep for the authorities, which it keeps until they have answered; that a notifier's name and email are kept apart from the case, never shown to staff or to the person reported, and deleted six months after the last day korbat still owed the report a decision or an email; how staff see a reporter or a notifier (a summary: roughly how old the account is, how many reports it sent, what share were acted on and how many were answered while their images could not be opened, in broad bands, never exact numbers) and when a moderator sees a reporter's handle or a notifier's name (only when a case needs it, for example a claim of impersonation or abuse of reporting, each time with a recorded reason shown to every staff member; the person reported never sees either); that korbat forgets which account sent a report 30 days after its last outcome was given and settled (at most about seven months after a decision to take no action, while it can still be re-examined); that on a report of child sexual abuse material staff see how many such reports about the same post, profile or author an admin answered without a seal in the last {SUSPECT_EARLIER_MONTHS} months, as a number and a day; that the account's export holds the decisions its case screens list and its own reports; and that a person who asks for their data at the address under Contact receives, within a month, every case about them (no-action cases included), the copies korbat keeps, where each case came from (a report by another user, a notice, a moderator) and, where the law requires it after weighing the writer's rights, the words of a report without who wrote it. The existing sentence of `terms.ts:31`, "At sign-in, Cloudflare Turnstile checks that you are not a bot", becomes "At sign-in, and when you send a report without being signed in, Cloudflare Turnstile checks that you are not a bot".

## 10. Contracts

`packages/contracts/src/moderation.ts`, exported from `src/index.ts`. Each table below is the one source its words and numbers are taken from: the console, the app, the mails, the terms and the README runbook use it, and a test pins each (P9, section 12).

- **Constants.** `TDB_CATEGORIES` (the 16 values of G9 2.5, read 2026-10-02), `TDB_FORM_CATEGORIES` (the 14 shown on the illegal-ground form: all but `STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC` and `STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE`), `CSAM_KEYWORDS` (`csam`, `deepfake`, `grooming` to their three keywords, and `abuse` to null), `RULE_DEFAULT_CATEGORY` (R1 `OTHER_VIOLATION_TC`, R2 `PROTECTION_OF_MINORS`, R3 `ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH`, R4 `DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS`, R5 `VIOLENCE`, R6 `SCAMS_AND_FRAUD`), `laneFor({ ruleId, allegesIllegal, csam, category })` (the lanes of section 2), `NOTICE_LIMITS` (5 and 20 signed out, 10 and 50 signed in, 10 items, 2000, 300), `CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS` (1: a notice on the CSAM path names at most one account), `SUSPECT_EARLIER_MONTHS` (12, the horizon of `suspicion.earlier`, 7.3), `SEAL_LIST_MAX` (500, the rows of a seal's list in the case answer), `APPEAL_MONTHS` (6, the author's appeal and the re-examination window), `DAILY_LIMITS` (five appeals a day per account; five re-examinations a day per account or network), `DECISION_KEYWORDS` (`KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT`), `MEASURES` (each `action_kind` with whether it is interim, final or a reversal, its target and its label for the composer, the statement and the terms), and `RETENTION` (the periods of 6.6: content restricted under R4 until its restriction is final, that is `APPEAL_MONTHS` after its author was told or the answer to their appeal (for a frozen post, until the freeze ends, 6.4); intake records 30 days after their last release, reset values 30 days after a lift that comes before the case's copies are erased, statements 12 months after the account's deletion, the access log and reveal reasons 12 months, notifier contacts six months after the last day owed and 13 months at most when nothing moved it, confirmations 30 days, backups 30 days after each was taken (`backupDays`; no code of 3c enforces it: the README tells the operator to delete older backups, except a backup that korbat must keep for the authorities, which it keeps until they have answered, and sub-project 4's backup job reads it), drafts 24 hours, mails given up after five days). The migration's CHECK lists are written from these constants, and a database test holds each such CHECK, as the migrated database defines it (`pg_get_constraintdef` over `pg_constraint`, which `korbat_api` can read), to exactly its constant's values, so the test still holds after a later migration replaces a list; a later list only adds values (6.1).
- **Digests.** `TEXT_DIGEST_TAG` (`korbat.text.v1`) and `textDigest(saltHex, text)`: the lower-case hex sha256 of the tag's bytes, a line feed, the salt's 32 bytes and the text's UTF-8 bytes (G1 5.1; the API, the console and `text-verify` call it; SQL's CHECK computes the same). `SNAPSHOT_DIGEST_TAG` (`korbat.snapshot.v1`), `snapshotText(snapshot)` (the sorted JSON of `{ v: 1, salt, targetType, targetId, takenAt, authorHandle, postState, postCreatedAt, replyToId, quoteOfId, body, media, displayName, bio, handle }`, with the sorted-JSON writer `stepUpActionText` uses, `sortedJson`, private today at `packages/contracts/src/staff.ts:250-266`) and `snapshotDigest(snapshot)` (sha256 of the tag, a line feed and that text). Every time in it (`takenAt`, `postCreatedAt`) is the UTC string that `Date.prototype.toISOString` writes, to the millisecond, as the snapshot answer carries it. `appealDeadline(informedAt)`: six calendar months later in UTC with the month-end clamp. The sorted-JSON writer and the `sha256` helper with its `WebPlatform` interface (`staff.ts:285-297`) move to a module of their own, `packages/contracts/src/canonical.ts`, which `staff.ts` and `moderation.ts` both import and `index.ts` need not export. `staff.ts` imports `moderation.ts`'s constants for the step-up params; `moderation.ts` imports nothing from `staff.ts`: `index.ts` evaluates `./moderation` before `./staff`, so a cycle between them would make `staff.ts`'s schemas read `moderation.ts`'s constants before they are initialised and fail at load.
- **App requests and answers.** `NoticeTarget` (`{ kind: "post", id, mediaId? } | { kind: "account", handle } | { kind: "link", url }`, the url at most 300 characters); `NoticeRequest`, a union by `ground`: `{ ground: "rule", ruleId, targets, explanation?, turnstileToken? }`, `{ ground: "illegal", targets, category, citedLaw?, explanation, bonaFide: true, ruleId?, name?, email?, turnstileToken? }`, `{ ground: "csam", targets, keyword, explanation?, bonaFide?: boolean, turnstileToken? }`, every text under `text.ts`'s rules without a transform; the rule variant's `ruleId` and the illegal variant's `ruleId?` are each one of R1, R3, R4, R5, R6; the CSAM variant's `keyword` is one of the four keys of `CSAM_KEYWORDS`; `NoticeResponse { ref, token? }`; `NoticeStatusRequest { ref, token }`; `NoticeStatus { ref, receivedAt, items: [{ position, link, scope, suspect, sealed, unseen, quotedBy, outcome, decidedOn, changed, reexamines, reexamination: { open, until } | null }], contact: { given, confirmed: boolean | null, stopped: boolean | null } | null }` (`outcome` and `decidedOn` null until released; `position` 1 to 20; `link` the item's korbat address, an account's built from the handle as the notice or report named it and never from the handle the profile holds now (7.2); `scope` `"account"`, `"quote"`, `"account_suspect"` or null, by which the page and the app add `ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE`, `QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE` or `ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE` after the outcome; `suspect` true for a suspect item, whose outcome is worded from `SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES`; `sealed` true, once released, when the item's answering decision holds `seal_media`; `unseen` true, once released, for an item about a post that is not suspect and whose answering decision's `unseen` is true, read from `decisions.unseen` and the item's own `suspect` (the decision was taken while nobody could open the post's images, 6.2 step 6), by which a `no_violation` or `not_evident` outcome is worded with `UNSEEN_NO_ACTION`; `quotedBy` the position of the item it was added for, for an item korbat added for a quoted post, else null; `changed` true when a review or a correction changed the outcome; `reexamines` true for a re-examination's item; `reexamination` null for an item that cannot be re-examined (answered without a decision, answered with any outcome but `no_violation` or `not_evident`, or itself a re-examination, unless it reads `UNSEEN_NO_ACTION`, 7.2), and otherwise `open` as 7.2 defines it and `until` the window's end; `confirmed` and `stopped` null unless the request carried the contact's mail token); `NoticeContactRequest { ref, token, choice: "confirm" | "stop" }`; `NoticeReexamineRequest { ref, token, position, statement? }` (`position` 1 to 20); `ReexamineRequest { statement? }`; `AppealRequest { statement? }`; `AuthorCasesPage`; `DecisionView` (the statement's data: kind, outcome, ground, rule id and version, legal reference, facts, reason, source (`notice`, `report` or `own_initiative`), measures with their scope and `noEffect` (`null`, `"already"` or `"deleted"`) and, for a `seal_media`, `sealed: { posts, images, deletedImages }` from `seal_posts`, reversals with the measure each lifts, `endedMeasures` (for a decision with `ended_interim`, the measures taken while deciding that ended with it; a seal taken while deciding is left out when the decision itself holds `seal_media`, since the images stay sealed), and, on every reversal or ended measure that is a field reset, `resetDecisionId` (the decision holding the reset: a reversal's `reviews_decision_id`, or the interim decision of an ended measure) and `oldValueKept` (true when that reset's `no_effect` is null and that decision's snapshot's `erased_at` is null or later than this decision's `decided_at`), decided at, `appealUntil` (the author's deadline, `appeal_deadline(informed_at)`, while an appeal is open by `appeals_check`'s rule, else null), `reversedOn` (only for a `final` decision with outcome `restricted`: the UTC day of the reversal row that lifted the last of its measures; null while any of them is in force, and for every other decision, an interim one included, whose measures end with their case without a reversal), `post` (`{ id, createdAt }` of the post its case is about, read from `posts`, whose id and `created_at` survive deletion, the purge and the redaction; null for an account case; never withheld by `snapshot_withheld`), the content actioned or the reason it is not shown (`r4_redacted`, `erased` with `contentErasedOn`, the UTC day of the snapshot's `erased_at`, and for images `sealed` and `deleted_by_author`; the first that applies, in that order), the appeal's state (`pending` or `answered`; for `pending`, `reviewer`: `"available" | "none_single_staff" | "none_eligible"`, the answer of `appeal_reviewer_state`, and `needsAdmin`, the answer of `review_needs_admin`: true only when the appealed decision cites R2 or sealed images, both of which its author was told) and the review's statement); `ReportsPage` (with `reportMailStopped: boolean`, 7.6; each item with `NoticeStatus`'s item shape, its `link` built the same way). `ItemOutcome` and `OUTCOME_PHRASES`, one phrase per outcome used by the mails, the status page and the app: `restricted_rule` "access restricted: it breaks korbat rule {rule} ({title})", `restricted_legal` "access restricted: korbat found it illegal", `no_violation` "no action: korbat found no breach of its rules and nothing illegal", `not_evident` "no action: korbat found no breach of its rules, and whether it is illegal cannot be seen without a detailed legal examination; a court or an authority can order its removal", `not_available` "no action: the link names nothing korbat can show (checked automatically)" (only for an item answered without a case), `partly_reversed` "korbat reversed part of its decision to restrict it", `reversed` "korbat reversed its decision to restrict it"; and `ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN`, added after a restricting outcome whose decision's measures all had `no_effect`: "It was already not shown on korbat, so nothing changed now; korbat's restriction stays in force should that change." (P2 law condition 1); and `ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE`, added after the outcome of an item whose target is an account, only when the item is not suspect and its answering decision holds no `seal_media` (every outcome but `not_available`), in the mails, on the status page and in the app's list as `ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN` is: "This answer concerns the account's display name and bio. korbat decides about its posts and images in cases of their own and does not report those here."; and `QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE`, added after the outcome of an item whose target is a post whose `quote_of_id` is set (every outcome but `not_available`; never for a suspect item, whose quoted post has an item of its own), in the mails, on the status page and in the app's list as `ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE` is, after `ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN` when both apply: "This answer concerns this post's own text and images. korbat decides about the post it quotes, shown inside its card, in a case of its own and does not report that here." On the path for child sexual abuse material nobody opens the images, so no item that a decision whose `suspect` is true answers, whether the item is suspect (6.1) or not, and no item about a post that a decision whose `unseen` is true answers without action, is shown words that say korbat found something about them. `SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES` holds two phrases in their place: `sealed`, for every item whose answering decision holds `seal_media`, suspect or not, since such a decision rests on images nobody opened (in place of `restricted_rule` and `restricted_legal`): "access restricted: korbat sealed its images without opening them. They are shown to nobody, their author included, and are kept for the authorities."; and `no_action`, for a suspect item answered `no_violation` or `not_evident` (in place of both): "no action: korbat's staff do not open images reported this way. An admin found in the report, and in what korbat can read and still holds of it, no sufficient ground to seal images or to restrict anything else.", which is true of a live image post, a text post, a deleted post and a purged account alike. A suspect item answered `restricted_rule` or `restricted_legal` by a decision that holds no seal (a measure on the post's text under another rule or the law) keeps that phrase, which is true of the text an admin read, followed by `SUSPECT_NO_SEAL`: "No image was sealed; korbat's staff do not open images reported this way." One more constant, `UNSEEN_NO_ACTION`, words an item on another ground that a decision answered with the images out of sight, and it follows from `decisions.unseen` alone (6.2 step 6: a final decision on a post case taken while the post was frozen, through a suspect item of its own case, through its author's account's case or through a seal in force): an item about a post that is not suspect and that a decision whose `unseen` is true answers `no_violation` or `not_evident` (the item's `unseen` is then true) reads, in place of those two phrases, as the `sealed` phrase replaces the two restricting ones: "no action for now: when korbat decided, its staff could not open this post's images, because a report of another kind about them was waiting or they were sealed. If your report is about an image, ask for a re-examination." So a moderator's no-action decision on text alone about a post that is frozen through its author's account's case, or whose images are sealed, tells its sender the truth and does not spend the re-examination. An item that reads it can be re-examined, also when it is itself a re-examination (7.2). An item about an account is never worded this way: when it is not suspect and is answered without action, it keeps the ordinary phrases with `ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE`, since its answer concerns the display name and bio, which staff read. `not_available`, `partly_reversed`, `reversed` and `ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN` (after a seal whose measures all had `no_effect`) are worded as for any item. `ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE` is added after the outcome of an item whose target is an account when the item is suspect or its answering decision holds `seal_media`, whether the item is suspect or not, since such an answer does concern the images on the account's posts (scope `account_suspect`; every outcome but `not_available`): "This answer concerns the account's display name and bio and, taken together, the images on its posts. korbat decides about single posts of the account, and about what its posts say, in cases of their own and does not report those here." An item korbat added for a quoted post is headed "The post that item {n} quotes ({link}), added by korbat", {n} its `quotedBy`. The `no_action` phrase and `SUSPECT_NO_SEAL` appear on the status page only, since a suspect item gets no mail (7.8); the `sealed` phrase, after it `ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE` for an item about an account, and `UNSEEN_NO_ACTION` also stand in a mail's line (the reporter's mail for a notice of illegality uses the same words) and in the app's list: the first two for an item of another ground that the sealing decision answered, the third for any item that reads it.

- **Step-up actions** (`packages/contracts/src/staff.ts`): `STAFF_STEP_UP_ACTIONS` gains `case_decided` (target type `case`), `appeals_reviewed` (target type `decision`) and `identity_revealed` (target type `intake_item`), each with a target id `LowerCaseUuid` and strict params of ids, enums, integers and 64-character lower-case hex only, never a free string and never a schema with a transform (repo-3c trap 1; `MediaId` transforms, so image ids are `LowerCaseUuid`): `CaseDecidedParams { kind: "interim" | "final" | "correction", stateVersion, throughSeq, reviewsDecisionId: uuid | null, snapshotId, snapshotDigest, outcome, ground: enum | null, ruleId: enum | null, rulesVersion, redressVersion, category: enum, categoryKeyword: "KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT" | null, actions: [{ kind, mediaId: uuid | null }] (at most 8), factsDigest, reasonDigest, legalReferenceDigest (each hex | null) }`; `AppealsReviewedParams { stateVersion, appealId: uuid, snapshotId, snapshotDigest, outcome: "kept" | "partly_reversed" | "reversed", rulesVersion, redressVersion, category: enum, actions: [{ kind, mediaId: uuid | null }] (reversals only, at most 8), reasonDigest: hex }`; `IdentityRevealedParams { reasonCategory, reasonDigest }`. Cross-field rules (the actions sorted by kind then media id, without repeats, at most one post measure (`withhold` or `remove`; a `seal_media` is none) and at most one `seal_media`; an interim decision's `throughSeq` 0; the outcome by kind (`interim` only `restricted`; `final` `restricted`, `no_violation` or `not_evident`; `correction` `partly_reversed` or `reversed`); `categoryKeyword` null unless `ground` is `illegal`; `ruleId` null when `ground` is `illegal`; a restriction's ground and digests; a correction's `ground`, `ruleId`, `categoryKeyword`, `factsDigest` and `legalReferenceDigest` null and its actions reversals only) are zod refinements, which keep no transform, and which zod 4.6.5's `.extend()` keeps when `requireStaffStepUp` adds `stepUp`, since its keys do not overlap (`node_modules/zod/v4/core/util.js:449-465`); the triggers check them again. `StaffStepUpOptionsRequest`'s union lists the three (`staff.ts:173`), and `packages/contracts/test/staff.test.ts:230`'s pinned keys become four. A schema test (C7) walks every params schema of the four actions and refuses any `z.string()` member that is not a uuid, an enum or a hex digest.

The routes may also answer the shared `invalid_request`, `onboarding_required`, `not_found`, `rate_limited`, `service_unavailable`, and on staff routes `staff_session_required`, `staff_step_up_required`, `staff_step_up_invalid`, `challenge_expired`, `csrf_failed`. Messages that the app shows are written for the person reporting or reported ("You already reported this; it is being looked at."), the console's for staff. The database-only codes `moderation_column`, `quote_item_missing` and `read_committed_only` are not among them: no route answers one, and no API path can meet one but the re-examination route, which runs its transaction once more on `quote_item_missing` (7.2).

`packages/rules/src/index.ts` gains `RULES_VERSION = 2`, `RULEBOOKS` (`{ 1: the six rules as they stand, 2: the six rules of section 9 }`), `RULES = RULEBOOKS[RULES_VERSION]`, `getRule(id, version)` and `REDRESS_VERSION = 1` with its three texts: korbat's appeal (with its deadline, the courts and the Digital Services Coordinator); the interim text, "This applies while korbat decides, and ends with its decision. If korbat's decision restricts your post or profile, you can appeal it. You can also go to court, or complain to the Digital Services Coordinator of the EU country where you live (Article 53 of the Digital Services Act)." (P5 law condition 2); and, for a decision its author cannot appeal, "korbat's appeal does not apply to this decision. Where an earlier decision about this content still stands in part, its own screen in korbat says whether you can still appeal it. You can go to court, or complain to the Digital Services Coordinator of the EU country where you live (Article 53 of the Digital Services Act)." 3e adds a redress version with an order's redress. `packages/rules/src/statement.ts` holds `statementParagraphs(input)`, a pure function of the decision's data (`DecisionView`), the rulebook version and the redress version, which the API's mail, the app and the console's preview share. It imports `DecisionView` and `MEASURES` from `@korbat/contracts`, which `@korbat/rules` depends on from Task 6. `@korbat/contracts` imports nothing from `@korbat/rules`, so the two packages never form a cycle. It picks the redress text from the decision's own kind and outcome, never from later events, so a statement renders as sent: an `interim` decision, the interim text; a `final` decision with outcome `restricted`, korbat's appeal; every other decision, the third text. A review or a correction renders the reviewed decision's rule or law from that decision's row and rules version, and its own redress under its own `redress_version`. It names the source as "following a notice under Article 16 of the Digital Services Act", "following a report by another user" or "found by a moderator". For every decision about a post, the sentence that says what was done names the post as "your post of {createdAt}", printed as `noticeTime` prints times. Its sentences, each true whatever happened later because none reads a later event (P1):
  - a `restore` or a `restore_media`: "korbat lifted this restriction. If your post or image is still restricted, another decision listed in Settings, Cases applies, or its content was erased under korbat's retention rules.";
  - a `restore_display_name` or a `restore_bio`: "korbat lifted the reset of your display name (bio).", then the field sentence;
  - a `reset_display_name` or `reset_bio` whose `noEffect` is null: "korbat wrote this placeholder once. You may set your display name (bio) again; what you set is judged on its own if someone reports it, and korbat does not put the old value back when this measure ends or is lifted.";
  - a measure with `noEffect` `already`: "Another decision already keeps this post (image) from being shown, so this changes nothing anyone sees now. It stays in force should that decision be reversed."; for a field, "The field already held korbat's placeholder, so this changes nothing now.";
  - a measure with `noEffect` `deleted`: "You had deleted this post, so this changes nothing anyone sees."; for a field, "Your account is deleted, so this changes nothing.";
  - a decision with `endedMeasures`: "What korbat did while deciding has ended: {measures}.", then the field sentence for each field reset among them whose field this decision does not reset itself;
  - the field sentence: "korbat does not put back your display name (bio) as it was before the reset: set it again in Settings, Profile if you wish.", followed, when `oldValueKept` is true, by "The screen of the decision that reset it shows what it was for at least 30 days." (when the reset is held by a decision citing R4: "The screen of the decision that reset it shows what it was for at least 30 days, unless korbat had already erased it under rule R4.");
  - a `seal_media` on a post case: "korbat sealed the images of your post of {createdAt} ({images} in all): nobody can see them, you included."; on an account case: "korbat sealed every image it held on your posts at that time ({images} on {posts} posts): nobody can see them, you included.", followed, when the seal lists posts the author had deleted, by "{deletedImages} of them are on posts you had deleted, which korbat had kept under its terms (Your data)."; the numbers are read from `seal_posts`. For a seal for good these are followed by "They are kept only for the authorities korbat reports this to." and, with the appeal's redress text, by "An appeal of a seal waits until the authorities have assessed the images.";
  - a `seal_media` with `noEffect` `already`: "Another decision already keeps these images sealed, so this changes nothing anyone sees now. It stays in force should that decision be reversed."; with `noEffect` `deleted`, the sentence of a deleted post or account above;
  - an `unseal_media`: "korbat lifted the seal on these images. If an image is still not shown, another decision listed in Settings, Cases applies."

`SEAL_DRAFTS` (`packages/contracts/src/moderation.ts`) holds the console's fixed drafts of the facts and the reason of a seal; the composer fills them in (section 8), and a test holds the composer and the preview to them (P9). None says or implies that korbat found the images to be child sexual abuse material, and each reason says that korbat's staff do not open such images, so that the statement meets Art. 17(3)(b) and (e) with what korbat knows. The facts: `facts.notice_post`, "korbat received a notice that reports images of this post as child sexual abuse material."; `facts.notice_account`, "korbat received a notice that reports this account for child sexual abuse material. It does not say which images, so korbat sealed every image on the account's posts."; `facts.notice_added`, "korbat received a notice about content on korbat that shows this post's images and reports them as child sexual abuse material."; `facts.finding_post`, "A moderator reported images of this post as possible child sexual abuse material."; `facts.finding_account`, "A moderator reported images on this account's posts as possible child sexual abuse material. korbat sealed every image on the account's posts."; `facts.finding_added`, "A moderator reported content on korbat that shows this post's images as possible child sexual abuse material." The two `added` drafts are for a case whose suspect items are all items korbat added for a quoted post: they never say that this post was reported, and they name no other post and no other person (T47). The reasons: `reason.deciding`, "korbat's staff do not open images reported this way, so korbat has not assessed them. It hides them from everyone, you included, until an admin has answered the report."; `reason.final`, "korbat's staff do not open images reported this way, so korbat has not assessed them. An admin found the report credible enough to keep the images sealed and to report them to the police, who can assess them." The facts draft is chosen from the suspect items the decision considers: a `notice` draft when any of them belongs to a `user` intake, else a `finding` draft; the `added` form when every one of them is an added item or a re-examination of one, else `post` or `account` by the case's target.

## 11. Security and privacy

What stays impossible even for an admin, in the API and the console, and what proves it (`threats-3c.md` section 6, as far as 3c's scope reaches; 3e carries the rows about suspensions, strikes and the orders path). Each row names the mechanism of sections 6 and 7 that enforces it and the test that proves it (P9).

- **Decide, review or reveal without a fresh assertion from one's own key bound to that exact action, case version and snapshot digest**: every such route stands behind `requireStaffStepUp` with strict params (section 10); `audit-verify` fails any row of the three actions without a valid assertion, whatever its actor (exists for every listed action, `apps/api/src/cli/staff.ts:332-334`); a route-table test requires every changing staff route to stand behind `requireStaffStepUp`, except the three named exceptions (saving a text, taking a snapshot, opening a finding) and 3a's enrolment, sign-in, step-up options and sign-out, listed by method and path.
- **Change a post's or an image's moderation state without a decision**: the ledger and its derivation (6.2): only `moderation_apply` writes the moderation columns, reachable only from the triggers of a decision inserted in the same transaction and bound to its audit row, and from the one-way erasure; the posts' trigger and the column grants (6.1). Database tests as `korbat_api`: a direct UPDATE of `posts.state` to `withheld`, `removed` or back to `visible`, of `moderation_level` or `erased_at`, and of `post_media.moderation_state`, `hold_until` or `erased_at`, refused; an insert into `seal_posts` refused; an INSERT of a post with another state or level or with `erased_at` set refused; leaving `deleted_by_author` refused for every role, the migrator included; EXECUTE on `moderation_apply` refused; an action inserted for a decision of another transaction refused, and one whose decision's stamped id a later transaction reaches after a logical restore refused by the time pairing; a decision without its audit row, and one whose case, decider, outcome, rule, digests or actions differ from its audit row's params, refused at COMMIT; and the function test of 6.5. `staff.js text-verify` also recomputes every post's level and every image's state from the ledger and reports any that differs (7.13), so a change made around the triggers is detected.
- **Change or delete an intake, item, decision, action, appeal, snapshot, text, hold or access row, or choose what a notifier is shown and when**: grants (UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE revoked; only the delivery columns writable); `release_outcomes` the only writer of `outcome_sent_at`, `shown_outcome` and `revised_sent_at`; database tests for each table as `korbat_api`.
- **Write a derived column of a case or a forced column of a decision**: forced or computed by the database (6.1, 6.2), `decisions.unseen` among them, so that no caller chooses whether an answer given while a post's images could not be opened says so; database tests.
- **Restrict without a ground, a reason, the facts and a snapshot, or without the author seeing it**: the checks on `decisions`, the consistency check at commit, `author_mail` forced; integration tests that the author's screen and mail carry every Art. 17(3) element for each outcome and measure, a measure that changed nothing now included (practice-3c 11.6).
- **Decide where one's staff account or a linked personal account is a party or related, review a case one decided in or opened a finding in, take a final restrictive measure on a staff account (an interim measure is allowed), answer a suspect item or an item citing R5 with a final decision of any outcome, lift a seal, correct a decision that needed an admin, or review a decision whose review needs one, as a moderator**: the decision triggers and the stored `needs_admin` (6.2, 6.3); an integration test for each, among them a moderator's correction that lifts a seal, and a final decision through an earlier suspect item while a later one of the case is unanswered, refused for an admin too (`case_changed`). And open a case, its images, snapshots or texts, or reveal a source in it, when its subject is one's own staff account, a linked personal account or an account related to them: `staff_case_conflict` before every case route and the reveal (7.3); an integration test per route.
- **Open an image of a frozen post, or a sealed image, as staff**: gate V (6.1, 7.3): `MediaForCases.staffImage` is the only function that opens an image file for staff, behind the one image route, and it refuses an image that is sealed or erased or whose post is frozen at the request, on every case, open or closed; the console's source test allows one image site. Integration tests (section 12): `staffImage` on the suspicion's own case, on another open case and on a closed case about the post, under each kind of reach (the post's own item, its author's account's item, an added item, a seal), refused, and served again after an admin's answer without a seal. No gate proves that a staff member does not open the post in the app (below).
- **Lift the protection of reported images without every other staff member learning of it**: `moderation_csam_lifted` after the commit of every decision that lifts a seal (`unseal_media`) and of every final decision that answers a suspect item without a seal, both an admin's by the triggers, and the home screen's 30-day list; and, so that a seal and a refusal to seal are as visible as a lifting, the home screen's lists of the seals taken while deciding that are in force and of the recorded choices not to seal (7.3, 7.5 step 4, 7.12, section 8); integration tests (section 12).
- **Show a sealed image to anyone, its author included**: gate S (6.1, 7.10): `moderation_apply` is the only writer of an image's state, and `fileAccess` behind `serve`, `forPosts`, and `readyImages` with the export's second read, name what they serve; one test per reader of `post_media` with a sealed image, its author signed in, over the one enumeration of the readers that section 12 holds (Every reader of an image: `serve`, each list behind `forPosts`, the export's files with an export in flight, `status` and `staffImage`); none gives the file, and none the `blurhash` (section 12; P1 law condition 1, security condition (a)). Text is not sealed, so no reader of `posts.body` has a rule for it. Up to five minutes of edge and browser cache remain after a seal until 3d's purge (below).
- **Put a reporter's identity, a report's words or a count into anything the author sees**: the author's reads never join `intakes` or `intake_items` (a source scan refuses the names `intakes`, `intakeItems` and `intake_items` in `author.ts`, `author-repo.ts` and `statement.ts`; and an integration test seeds a report and a re-examination whose reporter's handle, explanation and statement are distinctive strings, restricts the post, and finds none of them, nor the number of reports, in `GET /api/moderation/cases`, `GET /api/moderation/decisions/:id`, the post's chip, the export's `decisions` member or the `moderation_decision` mail); the overlap check on staff texts, re-examination statements included (unit tests); the statement names only a source category.
- **See a reporter's or notifier's identity without a recorded, confirmed reason visible to every staff member**: the reveal route (7.3: the party check, the reason text, the access row and the audit row in one transaction, the identity read only after the commit; section 8's home list); the daily reveal limit and the `moderation_reveal` mail after every reveal; no staff answer carries an address (the route-table test's `PERSONAL` over the new schemas).
- **Read email, IP, device or phone data, blocks, mutes, likes or bookmarks in the console**: the module boundary (the moderation module imports no auth-schema name; architecture test) and the answer schemas; the recusal check reads relations inside a definer function and answers one boolean.
- **Search freely, export in bulk, or download evidence in the console**: no such route (route-table test); evidence leaves the server only through the command line, in 3c what `staff.js account-facts` and `staff.js access-request` print, each with an audit row, and, for the files of sealed images, by the operator's hand as the server's administrator, on an authority's written instruction and recorded off the server (runbook, Task 12(a)); productions for authorities are 3e's (C38).
- **Act on Explore alone or reduce reach**: no action kind for it (section 6); 2c's tests unchanged.
- **Write personal free text into the chain**: the params schemas (the C7 schema test) and the digests; `text-verify` proves held texts are the confirmed ones.
- **Give effect to an authority's order, or mark a decision as one, from the console or the API**: no order path exists in 3c (7.14): `FindingRequest` has no other ground than a rule (a contracts test), `intakes_finding_legal` refuses a finding alleging illegality (a database test as `korbat_api`), and `decision_source` has no `order` value.
- **Delete an image row of a frozen post or request its files, detach or re-own an image, erase a snapshot of a frozen post, or serve, list or export a kept image of a deleted post**: gate K (`post_media_keep` and `post_media_guard`, with no DELETE on `posts` or `profiles` for `korbat_api`), gate E (`erase_snapshots`, the only writer of `evidence_snapshots.erased_at`) and the image readers (6.1, 6.4, 7.9, 7.10); the same trigger keeps every image a case's hold retains, and the disposal predicate deletes what nothing retains. Integration tests (section 12): every method of the media repository against a frozen post under each kind of reach, by enumeration, so that a new method fails until it is listed; the races of a suspect intake against the author's deletion and the purge, in both orders; a cascade as the migrator raising; a delete under REPEATABLE READ refused; an update of `post_id` or `owner_id` refused for every role; every step of the retention job and an R4 redaction leaving a frozen post's rows and snapshots; that `existing()` still sees retained rows; that a deleted post's kept images are in no view, no export list and no export file, and that `status` answers their owner as for a row that does not exist; and an image an R4 redaction erased (by `remove_media`, and of a post-level removal) that another case still holds answers 404 to its author and to the staff image route, is absent from `forPosts` and the export's list and files, and a later report about its post places no hold on it and copies no alt text. The pins of 6.5 and of the architecture test hold who names the predicate, who deletes from `post_media`, and every caller of `requestDeletion` and `openImage`.
- **Act beyond the daily decision cap**: the decision trigger; integration tests, among them two concurrent decisions by one person at the cap's last place, of which exactly one commits.
- **Write transparency figures**: no table and no route (3d's).

In the database, for `korbat_api`: no UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE on any moderation table but the delivery columns, no UPDATE of the moderation columns of `posts` and `post_media`, no DELETE on `posts` or `profiles`, SELECT only on `seal_posts`, no write to `audit_head` (exists), no USAGE on `auth` (now pinned by a test), SELECT on `measures_in_force` and `case_history`, and EXECUTE only on `append_confirmed_audit`, `appeal_deadline`, `frozen_for`, `post_frozen`, `snapshot_withheld`, `release_outcomes`, `decision_final_at`, `case_evidence_due_at`, `intake_due_at`, `appeal_reviewer_state`, `review_needs_admin`, `staff_case_conflict`, `erase_case_evidence`, `erase_intake`, `erase_statement_texts`, `redact_r4_body`, `sweep_staff_texts`, `delete_access_log` and `forget_reporter` (each granted in its own migration; a function-privilege test lists them, as `apps/api/test/integration/staff-schema.test.ts:383-399` does for 3a's). `moderation_apply`, `item_current_outcome`, `release_case_holds` and `erase_snapshots` have EXECUTE granted to nobody. `korbat_auth` gains EXECUTE on `auth.staff_link_counts` only, and the same test lists it (owner `korbat_migrate`, definer, `search_path=auth, pg_temp`, EXECUTE to the auth role alone). Each erasing function checks its own retention condition against values `korbat_api` cannot set: forced times, release times only `release_outcomes` writes, and an account's deletion read from `auth.users`, whose mark the API's other role, `korbat_auth`, can set only to `now()` and never clear (`users_deleted_mark`, 6.4); so the API cannot erase early. `redact_r4_body` checks the decision's kind, rule, measures and finality, and whether its post is frozen, itself, so a call with any other decision, before finality or while the post is frozen, changes nothing; it, `erase_snapshots` and the keep trigger refuse to act outside READ COMMITTED (6.1). `forget_reporter` needs only the mark, so code running as the API can forget a live account's reporter links only by marking it deleted for good, which the purge then completes. For the migrator, the superuser and anyone with Docker on the host, nothing is impossible; a change to a decision or its actions is detected by `staff.js text-verify`, which compares them with the audit row naming the decision, whose own changes the kept heads detect (3a section 2), and a change of a level or a state by its recomputation from the ledger; the other moderation tables are protected by grants only (G4 6).

**What the controls cannot prove.** The console's check of the step-up binding trusts the page, and the snapshot digest trusts the snapshot the API showed: an API compromised before a report can forge consistently from the start (T52's residual). The recusal check knows only the personal accounts the operator linked (T48's residual). An API under an attacker's control can learn whether an account is a staff member's linked personal account, or close to one: `korbat_api` may insert a case naming any account, or an intake whose reporter is any account, call `staff_case_conflict` on it, or insert a decision by any staff account and see whether step 5 raises `staff_recused`, and then roll back, leaving no row; on cases already in the table it needs no insert at all. `auth.staff_personal_accounts` keeps the link from every reader but the definer functions, not from code that runs as the API, which also holds `korbat_auth` and with it the hashed network address of every sign-in, staff sign-ins included (`auth.auth_events.ip_hash`). After an API incident the operator treats the links as known. A `staff_recused` refusal of a decision, or an appeal marked as not for this person to review, on a case whose subject is neither the moderator's linked account nor close to it tells the moderator that one of its reporters is close to their own account; with the source summaries, that can narrow down who reported (C20's residual). A reporter's summary is the same on every case they reported at that moment; its bands make it common to many reporters, but an unusual one (10 or more reports, none acted on) can still let a moderator who revealed that reporter once recognise them on other cases without a further reveal, and so can the wording of their reports (T44's residual). With one moderator, "a different human" is unavailable and appeals wait; a re-examination may be decided by the person who decided the original (section 2). Ids and times stay in the chain for ever (T56's residual). A notice's own text can identify its writer to staff (T44's residual). The freeze and the seal: anyone can freeze what a case reaches by sending a report of this kind through the report form, within the published limits, and an API under an attacker's control can freeze anything by inserting a suspect item; either is a denial of staff viewing and of deletion and, with the viewing, of every other procedure about those images until an admin answers (6.1, the freeze; section 2, the path's row). Such an API can also read any stored file and request any file's deletion, frozen or sealed, until 3d's quarantine (`apps/api/src/media/files.ts:181`; the worker obeys every request and has no database); it can rewrite `posts.body`, which the snapshot of a post case copied and an account case did not; and it can record a decision with a confirmation it made up, an admin's answer or `unseal_media` included, which `audit-verify` detects afterwards and nothing in the database prevents. It cannot delete a frozen row, change an attached image's alt text, or erase a frozen post's snapshot. Before a seal only the rule that staff never open a reported post or account in the app (6.1, the freeze) keeps a staff member from seeing a reported image there, nothing on the server records a look in the app, and after a seal the app still shows what the case does not reach: other accounts' images that a reported account reposted or quoted, the post a reported post replies to and its replies, which the post's page shows with their images, and images posted since the seal. A notice on another ground, or a rule report, whose words describe such images is not suspect until someone opens a finding citing R2 (runbook), so staff can open its images until then. The status page of a notice on this path shows a deleted post's item as waiting where a link that names no row is answered automatically, which tells whoever holds the token that the id exists (T43); an item that names an account by a handle it has left waits the same way, which tells that the handle still names an account and never which handle that account holds now (7.2). On every other ground an old handle is stored as an item whose id names nothing, and such links are de-duplicated by their named handles, so neither a stored id nor a de-duplication ties it to its account (7.1 step 4). A table added later that holds images (3b's import, 2d's avatars and share cards) must join a gate: the enumeration tests fail on a new method of the media repository, not on a new table. `text-verify` detects a sealed image row that the migrator destroyed or a restore lost (7.13). A removed or sealed image stays at Cloudflare's edge and in browsers for up to five minutes until 3d's purge.

**Privacy.** Notifier contacts live in the auth schema, encrypted, out of the API role's reach, and are deleted on a published schedule; a signed-in notifier's contact is their account. The CSAM path stores no account and no contact; its limits count in Valkey only (whether that is identification data is on counsel's list, G9 5.3). The access log records staff, not users. Reporter summaries are computed from the reporter's own rows, which their export contains (G9 3.9). The logger gains `salt` and `token` (already) among its redacted keys (`apps/api/src/lib/logger.ts:11`), so neither a text's salt nor a notice token reaches a log; the status page's tokens travel in a POST body, and the mail's link puts the mail token in the address's fragment, which no server log sees.

## 12. Testing

- **Unit**: the contracts' digests (`textDigest` against vectors shared with the SQL CHECK test, including texts with line feeds, non-ASCII text, emoji and the longest text; `snapshotDigest` round-trips the snapshot answer's JSON); `appealDeadline` against PostgreSQL's `appeal_deadline` on every month end of two years, a leap year included; `laneFor` over every rule, category and the CSAM path; the reporter summary's bands at each boundary (1 and 12 months; 1, 2, 9 and 10 items; no decided item, none acted on, just under half and exactly half; an item that reads `UNSEEN_NO_ACTION` counted in `answeredUnseen` and left out of the decided ones, so that a reporter whose only answered item reads it is `none_decided`) and its letters given per case; `NoticeRequest`'s strictness (refused: a CSAM notice with a name, a signed-in notice with an email, eleven targets, a CSAM notice with two `account` targets, an off-pattern link, a rule report or an illegal-ground notice citing R2; accepted: a rule notice with a `turnstileToken`, a CSAM notice without explanation or bona fide, a CSAM notice with keyword `abuse`); the step-up params schemas (strict, no transform, refinements kept through `.extend({ stepUp })`, unsorted or repeated actions refused, two post measures refused, a correction that carries a ground or facts refused, a final `kept` or `reversed`, an interim `no_violation`, a correction `restricted` and a review `restricted` refused, a review holding a measure refused, `categoryKeyword` with a rule ground refused, the C7 walk); `FindingRequest` refusing every ground but a rule; link parsing (`links.ts`: hosts, paths, case, trailing slashes, a handle that is not a handle); the overlap check (`overlap.ts`: whitespace, case, a 31-character run allowed, 32 refused, notes and `seal_declined` texts exempt, re-examination statements covered); `statementParagraphs` for every outcome, ground, measure and kind, both rulebook versions and the redress text each kind and outcome gets, each with the six Art. 17(3) elements present (practice-3c 11.6), among them an interim decision with the interim text, a correction of an interim decision, a final no-action decision that ends measures taken while deciding, the `restore` and `restore_media` sentences, the field-restore sentence and the field sentence after an interim reset ended by a closing decision, each with and without its 30-day sentence, and none for a field the closing decision resets itself, each `noEffect` sentence, and the seal's sentences for a post case and an account case, with and without deleted posts, while deciding and for good, with the waiting sentence of a seal for good; `reversedOn` null for an interim decision whose measures ended with its case; the WebP header check (a RIFF that is not WEBP, each chunk kind, an oversize edge, a size that differs from the row's); the console's pure parts (router with case paths, `parseCaseId`, `staffImageSrc`, the draft slot, the params builder, the hidden-characters view); the architecture test's new module and rules, each with a test that catches a deliberate violation; source scans: the console's two link sites and one image site, and the author-side files never naming the intake tables (section 11); `postAccess` over every stored state; `smtpMailer`'s errors: `EENVELOPE` on `RCPT TO` with `550 5.1.1 <a@b>: Recipient address rejected: User unknown`, with `550-5.1.1` on the first line of a multi-line reply, and with `556 5.1.10` is `MailRefused`; `RCPT TO` with `554 5.7.1 <a@b>: Relay access denied`, with `553 5.1.8 <f@g>: Sender address rejected`, with a bare `550 rejected`, and with 450, `MAIL FROM` with 550, `EAUTH` with 535, `EMESSAGE` on `DATA` with 554 and `ECONNECTION` are plain `MailUnavailable`; `smtpTransportOptions` sets `connectionTimeout` 10000, `greetingTimeout` 10000, `socketTimeout` 30000 and `dnsTimeout` 10000 for `smtp://` and `smtps://` URLs (the two existing cases in `apps/api/test/mail/smtp.test.ts` gain the four members).
- **The tables (P9)**: `OUTCOME_PHRASES` has exactly one phrase per `item_outcome` value, `ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE` follows the outcome of exactly the items about an account that are not suspect and whose answering decision holds no `seal_media`, `QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE` of exactly the items that are not suspect about a post whose `quote_of_id` is set, and `ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE` of exactly the items about an account that are suspect or that a decision holding `seal_media` answered, a rule report merged into a sealed account case among them; a suspect item is worded from `SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES` and never from `OUTCOME_PHRASES`' four words for a finding alone (`no_violation`, `not_evident`, `restricted_rule` and `restricted_legal` without `SUSPECT_NO_SEAL`); an item about a post that is not suspect and that a decision whose `unseen` is true answered `no_violation` or `not_evident` is worded with `UNSEEN_NO_ACTION` and never with those two phrases, on the status page, in the app's list and in a mail's line alike, and no other item is; `SEAL_DRAFTS` holds its eight texts, and the console's composer and the preview are held to them; the app's and the console's message tables have one entry per `ModerationErrorCode` they can meet; the terms' moderation sections, rendered, name every `MEASURES` label, every outcome phrase's meaning and every number of `NOTICE_LIMITS`, `CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS`, `SUSPECT_EARLIER_MONTHS`, `DAILY_LIMITS` and `RETENTION`, and no measure or period the constants lack (a strike, a retired handle, an order's preservation); and, in Task 12, a docs test holds the README moderation section's numbers (limits, response times, periods) to the same constants.
- **Integration (database)**, as `korbat_api` unless said, and run on a fresh database and on one migrated to 0013 and committed before the later migrations run as one batch (section 6; `scripts/test-db.mjs --fresh` and `--upgrade-from 13`, Task 1):
  - every grant and refusal of 6.5, and the function pins of 6.5; each CHECK written from a contracts constant held to its constant with `pg_get_constraintdef`; the forced columns ignoring supplied values;
  - the attach trigger (G3 L3 to L12 as tests: two first reports merging, a report against a closing case retried into a new one, opposite-order notices sorted, the naive path retried, the reporter-once index (a second rule report by one reporter on one case refused; that reporter's later illegal-ground notice on the same case accepted), no-case items only `not_available`); re-examination items accepted for a released no-action item within its window, with the original's target, position and lane whatever was supplied, and refused (`reexamination_not_open`) for a restricted item, an unreleased one, a re-examination, one past its window with the clock moved, and an erased intake; a second refused (`reexamination_exists`); a re-examination racing `erase_intake` in both orders: refused, or the erasure refused (`not_due`); `suspect` forced from the intake whatever was supplied; `named_handle` forced null for a post target whatever was supplied, kept for an account target and copied to a re-examination, and an account item without one refused by `intake_items_named_handle` (Task 1); `intake_items_quote`: a suspect item on a quoting post alone refused at commit (`quote_item_missing`), with the quoted post's item committed, an added item without its origin refused, a re-examination and a link that names no row passing, and a re-examination of an origin refused without one of its added item when that is open to re-examination;
  - the checks of `intakes` (a CSAM intake with `alleges_illegal` true and neither explanation nor bona fide accepted, an illegal-ground notice without them refused; a CSAM intake with a null keyword accepted, and one with a reporter or a contact refused; a user intake citing R2 refused, signed in or out, a finding citing R2 accepted; a finding alleging illegality refused);
  - a snapshot written by the intake transaction and one written by the snapshot route recompute from their stored rows to their digests; a capture of a post whose `erased_at` is set holds an empty body and null alt texts and is shown, not withheld, by `snapshot_withheld`;

Each task is one commit, written tests first, dry-run in the scratch clone with the gated runner, and leaves the stack working.

12. **Documentation.**
    - (a) The README's moderation section: how reports and notices arrive; the queue and its lanes with their response times (7.12: 24 hours in lanes 0 and 1, seven days in lane 2; targets for a team of one or two, not promises; staff get the queue-age mail when a case passes them, or when a measure taken while deciding is older than 24 hours); deciding and the preview; measures on content that is already not shown (recorded, told, in force should the other restriction be reversed); the limits on staff (the decision caps, the daily case-open, findings and reveal limits, all set with `staff.js limits`; every reveal, and every decision that lifts the protection of reported images, is mailed to every staff account); reveals; appeals and the one-moderator rule; re-examination (when the item re-examines your own decision and another staff member exists, leave it to them); evidence and its retention by consumer; the emergency switch (set `API_MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN=on` in `infra/.env`, then run `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d api`, which recreates the API with it, since the API reads it at start; `off` and the same command end it); the mails (the urgent-lane alert repeats about every 20 minutes until a decision answers the item or withholds the post in the interim; on a post already withheld, removed or deleted by its author, and on an account case, it stops once someone saves a note on the case after the item arrived, normally the Art. 18 check, and the case then waits for its final decision, an admin's for suspect items and items citing R5, under the queue-age mail; on a report or finding of child sexual abuse material whose case reaches an image that is still served it repeats until the images are sealed, someone records that they do not seal, or an admin answers, and starts again when an image is posted afterwards that the case reaches, and where its case reaches no served image a note or a decision taken while deciding ends it too (7.12); a mail is not a pager); and `staff.js link`, `unlink`, `limits`, `text-verify`, `account-facts` and `access-request`. It gives the rotation rule for `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY` beside the TOTP one (`README.md:174`): "To rotate `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY`, put the old key in `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS` and a new `v2:` key in `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY`. Contacts are never re-encrypted, so the old key stays listed until no contact made under it remains, that is until `select count(*) from auth.notifier_contacts where name_enc like 'v1:%' or email_enc like 'v1:%'` answers 0. A contact can outlive 13 months while its notice is still owed a decision or a mail. Keep the old key off the server for as long as any backup holds such a contact."
      Its runbook:
      - linking each staff member's personal accounts at onboarding and whenever they say they opened another;
      - **Reports and findings of child sexual abuse material (R2)**: nobody opens the images such a report concerns, in the console or in the app, before or after a seal, until an admin has answered without one. As soon as the urgent mail arrives, whoever has the server runs `staff.js account-facts` for the case's subject and keeps its output with the R2 records until the admin's answer; it is destroyed after an answer without a seal, and the seal never waits for it. Whoever is on duty opens the case and seals what it reaches with "Seal the images this case reaches", under rule R2, with the composer's drafts, and never writes that the images are such material. They seal unless the report is plainly unfounded, and then record why with "Do not seal now": an earlier answer without a seal was as unseen as this one will be, so it is a reason not to seal only when the report's words add nothing and the case reaches no image posted since that answer (the day of `earlier`'s last answer against the day of the newest post the case reaches) and staff have opened the images since the last answer (the case page shows the day for a post; for an account, a note or the colleague says so); a case that reaches no image cannot be sealed. A report about a post that quotes another has a second case, on the quoted post, linked from the first and sealed the same way. Nobody opens a post's page in the app while a report of this kind about the post is unanswered or its images are sealed (the rule of 6.1): it shows the post it replies to and its replies with their images, which the case does not reach. Nobody opens an account's profile in the app while a report of this kind about the account is unanswered or its images are sealed: it shows posts of other accounts that it reposted or quoted, which the case does not reach, and images posted since the seal; when the page shows images that are not sealed, whoever is on duty seals again. When the post's text links to or offers such material, the post is withheld as well. When the words of a report on another ground describe such images, whoever reads it opens a finding citing R2 on the post before opening any image. While such a report is unanswered, every other procedure about the same images (a report on another ground, a correction, the review of an appeal) is decided on text alone or waits for the admin's answer (6.1). A report about a post that is answered without action meanwhile, or while the post's images are sealed, is answered unseen, as the composer says there: its sender is told so and may ask again. An admin answers every such case, all its suspect items at once, without seeing the images: seal for good, and report, when the report's words, the post's text or alt texts, or the account's conduct give a concrete reason to believe the report; answer without a seal when they give none; say which it was in the decision's facts; in doubt, ask the operator before answering; never open the images to settle it. On a post's case the admin's answer also answers the reports on other grounds that arrived before the newest report of this kind, unseen; their senders are told so and may ask again (on an account's case such reports concern the display name and bio, which the admin reads). After an answer without a seal the case's images may be opened: whoever is on duty opens the case's target the same day (a post's images in the console, on its case; an account's in the app, which is then the only place they are shown, 6.1) and, where an image breaks a rule or the law, opens a finding on the post and decides it (if it is what the report said, a finding citing R2, which freezes again). For an account, and whenever a look found nothing, whoever looked writes a note on the case ("Images opened on <date> after the answer of <date>: nothing that breaks a rule"): the case page shows only the day a post's image was last opened in the console, nothing else on the server records a look at an account's images in the app, and the note goes with its case's evidence. When a new report of this kind arrives before that decision is made, the admin's next answer carries the measure for what staff saw, and its facts say when the images were seen. An admin's answer never restricts under another rule on a report's words alone about an image nobody at korbat has opened: that report is answered unseen, and its sender may ask again. An admin who can tell from an account report's words which post is meant opens a finding citing R2 on that post, seals there, and answers the account's item without a seal. An admin seals for good only what korbat then reports: on every seal for good the operator reports at once to the national police or the authority the Member State names, never to a hotline, with, for a post, its address, its times, the author's handle, the account facts and the text and alt texts of its snapshot, and, for an account, the handle, the account facts and the address, time and number of images of each post whose images are sealed, as the case page lists them (never an image). The operator records their reference with the address, the case and the seal's time, off the server, and tells them that korbat keeps the images sealed, that its software has no function yet to hand them over or to erase them, and that the operator does either by hand on their written instruction. On such an instruction, before sub-project 3d, the operator copies out or destroys the files of the sealed images by hand, as the server's administrator, without opening them (for a destruction, also every backup that holds them); the read-only query `select m.id from seal_posts s join post_media m on m.post_id = s.post_id where s.action_id = '<the seal's action id>' order by m.id` lists the images, whose files lie in the `media-store` volume under those ids; nothing in the database is changed, no admin lifts the seal for it, and the operator records off the server what was done, when and on which instruction. An admin lifts a seal for good only on the authority's answer that the images are not child sexual abuse material, and says in the reason that the authority has answered and the date of its answer, never its reference or anything that names a person (the reference stays in the operator's R2 records, off the server); a seal taken while deciding ends with the admin's answer, and before it an admin lifts it, by a correction, only when it was taken in error (on the wrong case, or on a report that the standard above gives no reason to believe). Every staff account is mailed `moderation_csam_lifted` after a lifted seal and after an admin's answer without a seal; the operator checks each against their R2 records and, when one was not expected, follows the mail's steps. A post already removed or deleted has its images sealed all the same (a seal of its own, P2);
      - a seal that lists more posts than the case page shows: the read-only query `select s.post_id, p.created_at, s.images from seal_posts s join posts p on p.id = s.post_id where s.action_id = '<the seal's action id>' order by p.created_at, s.post_id` gives every post the seal lists, with its creation time and its number of images, for the report;
      - a notice of illegality or any report about a post already removed or deleted is decided on its merits: a finding of a breach is recorded as a measure of its own;
      - a breach that lies only in a handle (impersonation, a doxxed name, a threat) is never answered "No breach" in 3c: the display name is reset when it carries the content, and otherwise the case stays open for 3e's handle retirement (its Art. 18 note ends the urgent-lane mails; the queue-age mail then reminds staff once a day) (P7 law condition 2);
      - **Art. 18 and TCO Art. 14(5)**: whoever on staff first reads a lane-0 case, or any case whose content suggests a threat to someone's life or safety, decides at once whether it gives rise to a suspicion of a criminal offence involving a threat to the life or safety of a person (DSA Art. 18(1); a suicide threat is not such an offence, `law-3c.md` 3.1, 3.4). If yes, or unsure, and they are not the operator, they wake the operator at once, at any hour. They record the check in a note on the case ("Art. 18 check: no suspicion" or "Art. 18 check: operator told at <time>"), and nobody gives such a case its final decision before that note exists. If yes, the operator informs promptly, at any hour, (i) the police of the Member State concerned (where the offence is suspected, or where the suspect or the victim lives or is), (ii) when that state cannot be identified with reasonable certainty, the police of korbat's own state, Europol, or both, through the channel obtained beforehand from the national police or the Digital Services Coordinator (`law-3c.md` 3.2), and (iii) for terrorist content with an imminent threat to life, the authorities of the states concerned, or else the home state's TCO Art. 12(2) contact point and Europol (TCO Art. 14(5), `law-3c.md` 3.5); the operator sends the content as the case page shows it, its publication time with the time zone, why it is suspected, the account's handle and what `staff.js account-facts` prints, and says what korbat does not keep (raw IP addresses, location) (`law-3c.md` 3.3); images reported as child sexual abuse material are never sent this way, and are reported as the R2 paragraph says; the operator records the authority, the channel, the basis for the state, the time, what was sent and the reference received, in their own records until 3e;
      - **authorities' orders before 3e**: the steps of 7.14; korbat stays private until 3e's order path and 3d's handling of sealed images have both shipped;
      - each January the operator counts the past calendar year's decisions marked terrorist content (with the reviews and corrections that reversed them) and the orders in their own records, and publishes the TCO Art. 7(2) report before 1 March when it applies;
      - **the users' contact mailbox**: the operator reads it at least each working day, in a mail client set to load no remote content and to show no inline image or attachment preview. Attachments are never opened, previewed, downloaded or forwarded, and no link in a mail is followed: a korbat link is copied into the report form, never opened. Every report or notice found there is entered through the report form, signed out in a private window, from the mail's text alone, with the sender's links, ground, rule or category, explanation and cited law, and, for a notice that is not on the CSAM path, the sender's name and email; the good-faith box is ticked only when the mail states the sender's good-faith belief that it is accurate and complete. It becomes a `user` intake of channel `signed_out`, so the sender gets `notice_received` with the status link, the daily `notice_update` and re-examination. A mail that says it concerns the sexual abuse or exploitation of a child, child sexual abuse material or the grooming of a child is entered on the CSAM path, with the choice its words name (`csam` when they name none) and without the sender's name or email. When the entered intake carries no contact (a rule-only report, or the CSAM path), the sender gets the fixed reply with the reference and the status page's link from the success screen. The mail is then deleted with its attachments and removed from the trash the same day; the fixed reply that carries a CSAM-path reference is deleted from the sent folder, and from the trash, once sent. A finding is never used for a mailed report or notice. A mail from an authority is handled under 7.14, its attachment opened only after 7.14 step 1 has verified the sender. No report or notice is answered by hand except with the README's fixed replies (one asking for the good-faith sentence or for the form; one giving the reference and the status link to a sender whose intake carries no contact; and one to a mail about a decision: "korbat answers a decision only through its own procedures: the person a decision restricts can appeal it in korbat under Settings, Cases, and a person who reported can ask for a re-examination of a decision to take no action on the page their receipt links to, or under Settings, Cases, Your reports, within six months of being told. korbat's emails never discuss a case."); the only other mails sent from this address are the GDPR answers (below) and the answers of 7.14; at most 20 can be entered a day from one network (7.1's limit), and while Turnstile is down they wait;
      - "illegal on the face of it" and when to answer "not evident" (`law-3c.md` 1.4, 1.6);
      - the statement's texts (facts, reason, legal reference, review reason) never hold personal data of anyone but the author: describe it ("the home address of another person"), never copy it, since they are mailed, exported and kept while the account exists, also after an R4 redaction has erased the content (`law-3c.md` 2.5 and its obligations table); a saved draft that copies it is not confirmed: save a corrected one;
      - machine translation stays local; the console in a browser profile of its own with no extensions, nothing pasted into third-party tools (C3); the daily case and reveal limits and raising them with `staff.js limits`;
      - a `staff_recused` refusal may mean one of the case's reporters is close to your own account: do not try to learn which, and leave the case to another staff member; when no other staff member can take it (with one staff member, always), the case waits in the queue and its lane-0 and queue-age mails keep coming, and the operator makes another person staff (grant-role and enrolment) to decide it; nobody unlinks an account, or unfollows, unmutes or unblocks one, to get round a refusal;
